value.zh: 家代重侯累相，靖安李氏，不在諸族之下；
value.en: For generations my house produced marquises and chancellors; the Jing'an Li are not beneath other clans;
value.literal: For generations my house produced heavy marquises and chancellors; the Jing'an Li family is not beneath the other clans;

value.zh: 論才較藝，何讓眾人。
value.en: in talent and skill, why should I yield to others?
value.literal: comparing talent and skill, why yield to others.

value.zh: 久置仆於朝行，諸君安乎？」
value.en: Keeping me so long in routine posts—are you at ease?"
value.literal: Long placing me in court ranks—are you gentlemen at ease?"

value.zh: 馮道、趙鳳每怒其僭。
value.en: Feng Dao and Zhao Feng were angered each time by his presumption.
value.literal: Feng Dao and Zhao Feng were each time angered by his presumption.

value.zh: 有頃，鏻因淮南細人言事，乃謂樞密使安重誨曰：「偽吳欲歸國久矣，若朝廷先遣使諭之，則旋踵而至矣。」
value.en: Soon, on a Huainan informer's report, he told An Chonghui, "Wu has long wished to submit; if the court sends an envoy, they will come at once."
value.literal: Before long, because of a petty man from Huainan reporting affairs, he told Military Affairs Commissioner An Chonghui: "False Wu has long wished to return to the state; if the court first sends an envoy to instruct them, they will come in a trice."

value.zh: 重誨然之，以玉帶與細人，令往淮南為信，久而不反，由是出鏻為兗州行軍司馬。
value.en: Chonghui agreed and gave the man a jade belt as envoy to Huainan; he never returned; Lin was sent out as Yan prefecture marching adjutant.
value.literal: Chonghui agreed, gave the petty man a jade belt to go to Huainan as envoy; he did not return for a long time; on that account Lin was sent out as marching adjutant of Yan Prefecture.

value.zh: 得代歸闕，復為戶部尚書，尋轉兵部尚書，有頃兼判太常卿事。
value.en: Returning to court he was again minister of revenue, soon minister of war, and before long acting director of imperial sacrifices.
value.literal: When his replacement returned to court, he was again minister of revenue, soon transferred to minister of war, and before long concurrently acted as director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

value.zh: 嘗權典選部，銓綜失序，物論非之。
value.en: He once ran personnel selection; his judgments were disorderly and opinion condemned him.
value.literal: He once held selection affairs in the Ministry of Personnel; his evaluation was disorderly and public opinion condemned it.

value.zh: 晉天福中，守太子少保。
value.en: In Jin's Tianfu era he was junior tutor of the heir apparent.
value.literal: In the Tianfu era of Jin he held the post of junior tutor of the heir apparent.

value.zh: 開運中，遷太子太保。
value.en: In Kaiyun he was promoted to grand tutor of the heir apparent.
value.literal: In Kaiyun he was promoted to grand tutor of the heir apparent.

value.zh: 高祖至闕，授守司徒，數月而卒，年八十八。
value.en: When Gaozu reached court he was made acting minister of works; he died several months later at eighty-eight.
value.literal: When the Gaozu reached court he was appointed acting Minister of Works; several months later he died at age eighty-eight.

value.zh: 詔贈太傅。
value.en: An edict posthumously made him grand tutor.
value.literal: An edict posthumously made him Grand Tutor.

value.zh: 職官誌
value.en: Treatise on Official Posts
value.literal: Treatise on Official Posts

value.zh: 梁開平三年三月，詔升尚書令為正一品。
value.en: In the third month of Kaiping 3 of Liang, an edict raised the Director of the Department of State Affairs to first rank, upper grade.
value.literal: In the third month of Kaiping 3 of Liang, an edict promoted the Director of the Department of State Affairs to the first rank, upper grade.

value.zh: 按《唐六典》，尚書令正二品，是時以將授趙州王镕此官，故升之。
value.en: Under the Tang Six Institutions the Director of the Department of State Affairs had been second rank, upper grade; the rank was raised because the post was about to be conferred on Wang Rong, military governor of Zhao.
value.literal: According to the Tang Six Institutions, the Director of the Department of State Affairs was second rank, upper grade; at this time the office was about to be granted to Wang Rong of Zhao prefecture, so it was raised.

value.zh: 梁書卷第十三 列傳第七
value.en: Book of Liang, Volume 13, Biographies 7
value.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 13, Biographies 7

value.zh: 齊初爲征虜記室，帶襄陽令，所奉之王，齊文惠太子也。
value.en: At Qi's opening he was campaign recorder with Xiangyang on his belt—the prince was Crown Prince Wenhuì.
value.literal: Early in Qi he was campaign-against-barbarians recorder, concurrent Xiangyang magistrate—the prince he served was Crown Prince Wenhuì.

value.zh: 太子入居東宮，爲步兵校尉，管書記，直永壽省，校四部圖書。
value.en: The heir moved east; he became infantry colonel, keeper of papers, stationed at Yongshou, collating the four library divisions.
value.literal: When the crown prince moved to the Eastern Palace, he was infantry colonel, in charge of records, on duty at Yongshou office, collating the four sections of books.

value.zh: 時東宮多士，約特被親遇，每直入見，影斜方出。
value.en: The eastern palace teemed with talent, yet Yue alone was drawn close—he walked straight in and left only when the sun hung low.
value.literal: Many scholars were at the Eastern Palace; Yue was specially favored, entering straight through each time and not leaving until his shadow slanted long.

value.zh: 當時王侯到宮，或不得進，約每以爲言。
value.en: Sometimes even kings and marquises were turned away at the gate, and Yue always pleaded their case.
value.literal: At times princes and marquises coming to the palace could not get in—Yue always spoke up about it.

value.zh: 太子曰：「吾生平懶起，是卿所悉，得卿談論，然後忘寢。
value.en: The heir said, "You know how late I like to wake; only your talk makes me forget the bed.
value.literal: The crown prince said: "I have been lazy to rise all my life, as you know; only when I talk with you do I forget sleep.

value.zh: 卿欲我夙興，可恒早入。」
value.en: If you want me at dawn, come early every day."
value.literal: If you want me up early, come in early every day."

value.zh: 遷太子家令，後以本官兼著作郎，遷中書郎，本邑中正，司徒右長史，黃門侍郎。
value.en: He rose to eastern-palace household head, then added compilation gentleman, secretariat gentleman, native impartial judge, right chief of staff to the minister of works, and yellow-gate companion.
value.literal: He was promoted to Eastern Palace Household Head, later combining that office with Compilation Gentleman, then Secretariat Gentleman, native-district impartial judge, Right Chief of Staff of the Minister of Works, and Yellow Gate Gentleman Companion.

value.zh: 時竟陵王亦招士，約與蘭陵蕭琛、琅邪王融、陳郡謝朓、南鄉范雲、樂安任昉等皆遊焉，當世號爲得人。
value.en: The Prince of Jingling too kept a salon; Yue moved with Xiao Chen, Wang Rong, Xie Tiao, Fan Yun, Ren Fang, and the rest—men of the age called them the company worth having.
value.literal: The Prince of Jingling also gathered scholars; Yue with Xiao Chen of Lanling, Wang Rong of Langye, Xie Tiao of Chen commandery, Fan Yun of Nanxiang, Ren Fang of Le'an, and others all associated—at the time they were called the attained men.

value.zh: 俄兼尚書左丞，尋爲御史中丞，轉車騎長史。
value.en: Soon he doubled as left assistant in the Masters of Writing, then censor-in-chief, then chief clerk to the cavalry general.
value.literal: Soon he concurrently served as Left Assistant Minister of the Masters of Writing, then became Censor-in-Chief, then Chief Clerk of the Cavalry General.

value.zh: 隆昌元年，除吏部郎，出爲寧朔將軍、東陽太守。
value.en: In the first Longchang year he took the personnel post, then left as pacify-the-north general and administrator of Dongyang.
value.literal: In Longchang year 1, he was appointed Department of Personnel Attendant, then went out as Pacify-the-North General and Administrator of Dongyang.

value.zh: 明帝卽位，進號輔國將軍，徵爲五兵尚書，遷國子祭酒。
value.en: Ming's accession brought him the title assist-the-state; he was called to armaments minister, then made chancellor of the imperial academy.
value.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne, his title advanced to Assist-the-State General; he was summoned as Masters of Armaments Minister, then became Chancellor of the Imperial Academy.

value.zh: 明帝崩，政歸塚宰，尚書令徐孝嗣使約撰定遺詔。
value.en: When Ming died the regent held the reins; Xu Xiaosi ordered Yue to fix the final edict.
value.literal: When Emperor Ming died, power fell to the chamberlain; Minister Xu Xiaosi had Yue draft the death edict.

value.zh: 遷左衛將軍，尋加通直散騎常侍。
value.en: He became left guard general, soon with unimpeded transmission regular attendant added.
value.literal: He was promoted to Left Guard General, soon with added Unimpeded Transmission Regular Attendant.

value.zh: 永元二年，以母老表求解職，改授冠軍將軍、司徒左長史，征虜將軍、南清河太守。
value.en: In Yongyuan year 2 he begged off for his mother's sake and was shifted to champion general, left chief of staff, campaign general, and administrator of Southern Qinghe.
value.literal: In Yongyuan year 2, citing his mother's age he petitioned to leave office; reassigned as Champion General and Left Chief of Staff of the Minister of Works, Campaign General and Administrator of Southern Qinghe.

value.zh: 到沆 丘遲 劉苞 袁峻 庾於陵 弟肩吾 劉昭 何遜 鍾嶸 周興嗣 吳均
value.en: Dao Hang · Qiu Chi · Liu Bao · Yuan Jun · Yu Yuling · Jianwu (brother) · Liu Zhao · He Xun · Zhong Rong · Zhou Xingsi · Wu Jun
value.literal: Dao Hang, Qiu Chi, Liu Bao, Yuan Jun, Yu Yuling, younger brother Jianwu, Liu Zhao, He Xun, Zhong Rong, Zhou Xingsi, Wu Jun

value.zh: 肩吾字子慎。
value.en: Jianwu, styled Zishen.
value.literal: Jianwu, courtesy name Zishen.

value.zh: 八歲能賦詩，特爲兄於陵所友愛。
value.en: At eight he wrote verse and was Yuling's favorite brother.
value.literal: At eight he could compose poetry and was especially loved by his elder brother Yuling.

value.zh: 初爲晉安王國常侍，仍遷王宣惠府行參軍。
value.en: He began as Jin'an regular attendant, then prince Xuanhui army aide.
value.literal: He first served as Regular Attendant of the Jin'an princedom, then was promoted to Army Aide of the Prince's Xuanhui office.

value.zh: 自是每王徙鎮，肩吾常隨府。
value.en: Whenever the prince moved fief Jianwu followed.
value.literal: From then on whenever the prince moved his fief Jianwu followed the headquarters.

value.zh: 歷王府中郎、雲麾參軍，並兼記室參軍。
value.en: He was princely middle attendant, cloud-banner aide, and chief secretary.
value.literal: He served as princely middle attendant, Cloud Banner army aide, and chief secretary throughout.

value.zh: 中大通三年，王爲皇太子，兼東宮通事舍人，除安西湘東王錄事參軍，俄以本官領荊州大中正。
value.en: Zhongdatong year three the prince became heir; Jianwu was Eastern Palace courier and Xiangdong recorder, soon Jingzhou chief.
value.literal: In the third year of Zhongdatong the prince became crown prince; Jianwu was Eastern Palace courier while also Jin'an-Xiangdong recorder, and soon headed Jingzhou as chief.

value.zh: 累遷中錄事諮議參軍、太子率更令、中庶子。
value.en: He rose to central records consulting colonel, crown prince commissioner of seasons, and household vice-supervisor.
value.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to consulting colonel of the central records, Crown Prince Commissioner for Increasing the Seasons, and Household Vice-Supervisor.

value.zh: 初，太宗在籓，雅好文章士，時肩吾與東海徐摛、吳郡陸杲、彭城劉遵、劉孝儀、儀弟孝威，同被賞接。
value.en: In the fief Taizong loved writers; Jianwu, Xu Chi, Lu Guo, Liu Zun, Xiaoyi, and Xiaowei were favored.
value.literal: When Taizong was still in the fief he loved men of letters; then Jianwu with Xu Chi of Donghai, Lu Guo of Wu, Liu Zun and Liu Xiaoyi of Pengcheng, and Xiaoyi's brother Xiaowei were all favored.

value.zh: 及居東宮，又開文德省，置學士，肩吾子信、摛子陵、吳郡張長公、北地傅弘、東海鮑至等充其選。
value.en: As crown prince he reopened Wende scholars—Jianwu's Xin, Chi's Ling, Zhang Changgong, Fu Hong, and Bao Zhi among them.
value.literal: When he dwelt in the Eastern Palace he again opened the Wende office and placed scholars; Jianwu's son Xin, Chi's son Ling, Zhang Changgong of Wu, Fu Hong of Beidi, and Bao Zhi of Donghai were chosen.

value.zh: 齊永明中，文士王融、謝朓、沈約文章始用四聲，以爲新變，至是轉拘聲韻，彌尚麗靡，復逾於往時。
value.en: Qi Yongming brought four-tone verse; now rhyme grew tighter and ornament surpassed the past.
value.literal: In Qi Yongming, Wang Rong, Xie Tiao, and Shen Yue first used the four tones in writing as a new change; by now sound and rhyme grew stricter and ornate beauty exceeded the past.

value.zh: 時太子與湘東王書論之曰：
value.en: The crown prince then wrote Prince Xiangdong, saying:
value.literal: Then the crown prince wrote to the Prince of Xiangdong discussing it, saying:

value.zh: 興嗣世居姑孰。
value.en: The Xingsi clan lived at Gushu for generations.
value.literal: The Xingsi family for generations lived at Gushu.

value.zh: 年十三，遊學京師，積十餘載，遂博通記傳，善屬文。
value.en: At thirteen he studied in the capital; after ten-plus years he mastered records and wrote well.
value.literal: At thirteen he traveled to study in the capital; over more than ten years he came to master records broadly and was skilled at literary composition.

value.zh: 嘗步自姑孰，投宿逆旅，夜有人謂之曰：「子才學邁世，初當見識貴臣，卒被知英主。」
value.en: Walking from Gushu he lodged at an inn; at night a voice said: "Your learning surpasses the age; first eminent ministers will know you, then an outstanding lord."
value.literal: Once walking from Gushu he lodged at an inn; at night someone said to him: "Sir, your learning surpasses the age; at first you will be known to eminent ministers, and in the end favored by an outstanding lord."

value.zh: 言終，不測所之。
value.en: When it ended he could not tell where the man went.
value.literal: When the speech ended, he could not tell where the man went.

value.zh: 齊隆昌中，侍中謝朏爲吳興太守，唯與興嗣談文史而已。
value.en: In Qi's Longchang, Xie Tiao as Wuxing grand administrator discussed only literature and history with Xingsi.
value.literal: In Qi's Longchang era Attendant-in-ordinary Xie Tiao was Grand Administrator of Wuxing and discussed literature and history with Xingsi alone.

value.zh: 及罷郡還，因大相稱薦。
value.en: Leaving office he greatly praised and recommended him.
value.literal: When he left his post and returned, he greatly commended and recommended him.

value.zh: 本州舉秀才，除桂陽郡丞，太守王嶸素相賞好，禮之甚厚。
value.en: Recommended as Outstanding Talent, he became Guiyang assistant; Grand Administrator Wang Rong long admired him and treated him generously.
value.literal: The commandery recommended him as Outstanding Talent; he was appointed Assistant Administrator of Guiyang. Grand Administrator Wang Rong had long admired him and treated him with very thick courtesy.

value.zh: 高祖革命，興嗣奏《休平賦》，其文甚美，高祖嘉之。
value.en: When Gaozu took power, Xingsi submitted "Ode on Rest and Peace"—very fine, and Gaozu praised it.
value.literal: When Gaozu overthrew the old regime, Xingsi submitted "Ode on Rest and Peace"; its writing was very fine and Gaozu praised it.

value.zh: 拜安成王國侍郎，直華林省。
value.en: He became Prince Ancheng's gentleman and served straight at Hualin.
value.literal: He was appointed Gentleman of the Prince of Ancheng's state and served straight at the Hualin Office.

value.zh: 其年，河南獻儛馬，詔興嗣與待詔到沆、張率爲賦，高祖以興嗣爲工。
value.en: That year Henan sent tribute horses; Gaozu had Xingsi, Dao Hong, and Zhang Shuai compose fu and judged Xingsi best.
value.literal: That year Henan presented tribute horses; an edict had Xingsi and Attendant-at-Draft Dao Hong and Zhang Shuai compose fu; Gaozu regarded Xingsi's as best.

value.zh: 擢員外散騎侍郎，進直文德、壽光省。
value.en: He rose to cadet-attendant emeritus and served straight in Wende and Shouguang.
value.literal: He was promoted to Cadet-Attendant Emeritus and advanced to serve straight in the Wende and Shouguang offices.

value.zh: 是時，高祖以三橋舊宅爲光宅寺，敕興嗣與陸倕各制寺碑。
value.en: Gaozu made the Three Bridges old residence Guangzai Temple and ordered Xingsi and Lu Yan each to write a stele.
value.literal: At that time Gaozu made the old residence at Three Bridges into Guangzai Temple and ordered Xingsi and Lu Yan each to compose a temple stele.

value.zh: 及成俱奏，高祖用興嗣所制者。
value.en: Both were submitted; Gaozu used Xingsi's.
value.literal: When both were submitted Gaozu used the one Xingsi composed.

value.zh: 自是《銅表銘》、《柵塘碣》、《北伐檄》、《次韻王羲之書千字》，並使興嗣爲文；
value.en: Thence the bronze-column inscription, barrier-pond stele, northern expedition proclamation, and verse matching Wang Xizhi's Thousand Characters all went to Xingsi;
value.literal: From then on the Bronze Column Inscription, Barrier Pond Stele, Northern Expedition Proclamation, and verse matching Wang Xizhi's Thousand Characters were all entrusted to Xingsi for the text;

value.zh: 每奏，高祖輒稱善，加賜金帛。
value.en: each submission won praise and gifts of gold and silk.
value.literal: each time he submitted, Gaozu would praise it and add gifts of gold and silk.

value.zh: 九年，除新安郡丞，秩滿，復爲員外散騎侍郎，佐撰國史。
value.en: Year nine he became Xin'an assistant; after his term he again became cadet-attendant emeritus and helped compile national history.
value.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed Assistant Administrator of Xin'an; when his term expired he again became Cadet-Attendant Emeritus and assisted in compiling the National History.

value.zh: 十二年，遷給事中，撰文如故。
value.en: Year twelve he became supervisor of attendants, writing as before.
value.literal: In the twelfth year he was promoted to Supervisor of Attendants, composing documents as before.

value.zh: 興嗣兩手先患風疽，是年又染癘疾，左目盲，高祖撫其手，嗟曰：「斯人也而有斯疾也！」
value.en: Xingsi long had wind sores in both hands; that year plague came and his left eye went blind; Gaozu stroked his hand: "That such a man should have such illness!"
value.literal: Xingsi had long suffered wind sores in both hands; that year he also caught plague, his left eye went blind; Gaozu stroked his hand and sighed: "That a man like this should have such an illness!"

value.zh: 手疏治疽方以賜之。
value.en: Gaozu drafted a sore-treatment prescription by hand and gave it him.
value.literal: By hand he drafted a prescription for treating sores and bestowed it on him.

value.zh: 其見惜如此。
value.en: He was cherished thus.
value.literal: He was cherished thus.

value.zh: 任昉又愛其才，常言曰：「周興嗣若無疾，旬日當至御史中丞。」
value.en: Ren Fang loved his talent and said: "Without Zhou Xingsi's illness, within ten days he would reach vice censor-in-chief."
value.literal: Ren Fang also loved his talent and often said: "Were it not for Zhou Xingsi's illness, within ten days he would reach Vice Director of the Secretariat Censorate."

value.zh: 十四年，除臨川郡丞。
value.en: Year fourteen he became Linchuan assistant.
value.literal: In the fourteenth year he was appointed Assistant Administrator of Linchuan.

value.zh: 十七年，復爲給事中，直西省。
value.en: Year seventeen he again became supervisor of attendants, serving straight in the Western Office.
value.literal: In the seventeenth year he again became Supervisor of Attendants, serving straight in the Western Office.

value.zh: 左衛率周捨奉敕注高祖所制歷代賦，啓興嗣助焉。
value.en: Zhou She of the Left Guard received an edict to annotate imperial fu and asked Xingsi to assist.
value.literal: Leader of the Left Guard Zhou She received an edict to annotate the various fu composed by successive emperors as ordered by Gaozu, and memorialized that Xingsi should assist.

value.zh: 普通二年，卒。
value.en: In Putong year two he died.
value.literal: In the second year of Putong he died.

value.zh: 所撰《皇帝實錄》、《皇德記》、《起居注》、《職儀》等百餘卷，文集十卷。
value.en: He compiled Imperial Veritable Records, Record of Imperial Virtue, Daily Records, Rites of Office, and more—over a hundred juan—and ten juan of collected writings.
value.literal: What he compiled—*Imperial Veritable Records*, *Record of Imperial Virtue*, *Daily Records*, *Rites of Office*, and the like—totaled over a hundred juan, and his collected writings ten juan.

value.zh: 昭居寧夏十二年，老成持重，兵政修舉，亦會敵勢衰弱，邊境得無事。
value.en: Zhao held Ningxia for twelve years, steady and deliberate; military affairs were kept in good order, and as enemy strength waned the border remained quiet.
value.literal: Zhao resided at Ningxia for twelve years, steady and deliberate in bearing; military administration was well maintained, and it happened also that the enemy's strength waned, so the border knew no disturbance.

value.zh: 兵部尚書王驥、寧夏參將王榮嘗舉其過。
value.en: Minister of War Wang Ji and Ningxia assistant commander Wang Rong once reported his faults.
value.literal: Minister of War Wang Ji and Ningxia Assistant Commander Wang Rong once reported his faults.

value.zh: 朝議，以昭守邊久，習兵事，不易也。
value.en: At court it was held that Zhao had long guarded the frontier and knew military affairs too well to be replaced lightly.
value.literal: At court it was argued that Zhao had long guarded the frontier and was versed in military affairs—he should not be replaced lightly.

value.zh: 而與昭並為邊將最久、有勛績可稱者，都督同知劉昭鎮西寧二十年；
value.en: Among frontier generals who, like Zhao, had served longest with merit worth noting were Assistant Commissioner Liu Zhao, who garrisoned Xining for twenty years,
value.literal: Those who, like Zhao, had served longest as frontier generals with merit worth noting included Assistant Commissioner Liu Zhao, who garrisoned Xining for twenty years;

value.zh: 都指揮李達鎮洮州至四十年。
value.en: and Regional Commander Li Da, who held Taozhou for as long as forty years.
value.literal: and Regional Commander Li Da, who garrisoned Taozhou for as long as forty years.

value.zh: 並為蕃漢所畏服。
value.en: Both were feared and obeyed by Tibetans and Chinese alike.
value.literal: Both were feared and respected by Tibetans and Chinese alike.

value.zh: 南齊書卷四十六‧列傳第二十七
value.en: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 46 · Biographies 27
value.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 46, Biographies 27

value.zh: 廬江何點薦慧曉於豫章王嶷，補司空掾，加以恩禮。
value.en: He Dian of Lujiang recommended Huixiao to the Prince of Yuzhang, Yi, who appointed him aide on the staff of the Minister of Works and treated him with special favor.
value.literal: He Dian of Lujiang recommended Huixiao to the Prince of Yuzhang, Yi; he was appointed aide to the Minister of Works and accorded favor and ceremony.

value.zh: 轉長沙王鎮軍諮議參軍。
value.en: He was transferred to advisory military aide on the staff of the Prince of Changsha as General Guarding the Army.
value.literal: He was transferred to Advisory Military Aide on the staff of the Prince of Changsha as General Guarding the Army.

value.zh: 安陸侯緬爲吳郡，復禮異慧曉，慧曉求補緬府諮議參軍。
value.en: When the Marquis of Anlu, Mian, held Wu commandery, he again showed Huixiao exceptional courtesy, and Huixiao asked to serve as advisory military aide on his staff.
value.literal: When the Marquis of Anlu, Mian, was assigned to Wu commandery, he again treated Huixiao with special courtesy; Huixiao requested appointment as advisory military aide on Mian's staff.

value.zh: 遷始興王前將軍安西諮議，領冠軍錄事參軍，轉司徒從事中郎，遷右長史。
value.en: He was transferred to advisory officer on the staff of the Prince of Shixing as Forward General and General Pacifying the West, concurrently as Recorder on the staff of the Champion, then Attendant of the Minister of State Affairs, and finally Right Chief Clerk.
value.literal: He was transferred to advisory officer under the Prince of Shixing as Forward General and General Pacifying the West, concurrently Recorder on the staff of the Champion; transferred to Attendant of the Minister of State Affairs, then transferred to Right Chief Clerk.

value.zh: 時陳郡謝朏爲左長史，府公竟陵王子良謂王融曰：「我府二上佐，求之前世，誰可爲比？」
value.en: At the time Xie Tiao of Chen served as Left Chief Clerk; the Prince of Jingling, Ziliang, said to Wang Rong: "My headquarters' two senior aides—searching through past ages, with whom can they be compared?"
value.literal: At the time Xie Tiao of Chen commandery was Left Chief Clerk; the Prince of the headquarters, the Prince of Jingling, Ziliang, said to Wang Rong: "My headquarters' two senior aides—searching through past ages, with whom can they be compared?"

value.zh: 融曰：「兩賢同時，便是未有前例。」
value.en: Wang Rong replied: "Two such worthies serving together—that in itself has no precedent."
value.literal: Rong said: "Two worthies at once—that in itself has no precedent."

value.zh: 子良於西邸抄書，令慧曉參知其事。
value.en: Ziliang had books copied at the Western Lodge and put Huixiao in charge of overseeing the work.
value.literal: Ziliang had books copied at the Western Lodge and had Huixiao assist in overseeing the matter.

value.zh: 蠻
value.en: The Man.
value.literal: The Man.

value.zh: 高麗俗服窮袴，冠折風一梁，謂之幘。
value.en: Goguryeo custom favored narrow trousers and a cap with a single crosswise rib, called a ze.
value.literal: Gaoli custom: dress of narrow trousers, a cap with one crossbeam of folded wind, called a ze.

value.zh: 知讀五經。
value.en: They could read the Five Classics.
value.literal: They know how to read the Five Classics.

value.zh: 使人在京師，中書郎王融戯之曰：「服之不衷，身之災也。
value.en: When a Goguryeo envoy was in the capital, Secretariat Gentleman Wang Rong teased him, quoting, 'Dress that is not centered brings bodily disaster.
value.literal: When an envoy was in the capital, Secretariat Gentleman Wang Rong jested with him, saying: 'Dress not at the center is a bodily calamity.

value.zh: 頭上定是何物？」
value.en: What in the world is that on your head?'
value.literal: What exactly is that on your head?'

value.zh: 答曰：「此即古弁之遺像也。」
value.en: The envoy replied, 'This is the ancient ceremonial cap preserved from antiquity.'
value.literal: He answered: 'This is the surviving image of the ancient bian cap.'

value.zh: 王弘，字休元，琅邪临沂人也。
value.en: Wang Hong, courtesy name Xiuyuan, came from Langya commandery, Linyi county.
value.literal: Wang Hong, styled Xiuyuan, was a man of Langya Linyi.

value.zh: 曾祖导，晋丞相，祖洽，中领军，父珣，司徒。
value.en: His great-grandfather Dao had served as Chancellor of Jin; his grandfather Qia as Central Army Commander; his father Xun as Minister of Education.
value.literal: His great-grandfather Dao was Chancellor of Jin; his grandfather Qia was Central Army Commander; his father Xun was Minister of Education.

value.zh: 僧達孫 融
value.en: Sengda's grandson Rong
value.literal: Sengda's grandson Rong

value.zh: 融字元長，少而神明警慧。
value.en: Rong, courtesy name Yuanchang, was bright and precocious from childhood.
value.literal: Rong, styled Yuanchang, from youth was bright and keenly intelligent.

value.zh: 母臨川太守謝惠宣女，性敦敏，教融書學。
value.en: His mother was a daughter of Xie Huixuan, Administrator of Linchuan; earnest and quick herself, she taught Rong reading and scholarship.
value.literal: His mother was daughter of Xie Huixuan, Administrator of Linchuan; she was earnest and quick, and taught Rong letters and learning.

value.zh: 博涉有文才，從叔儉謂人曰：「此兒至四十，名位自然及祖。」
value.en: Well read and gifted in letters, his father's younger cousin Jian told others: "At forty this boy will naturally match his grandfather in rank and fame."
value.literal: Broadly read and possessed of literary talent, his father's younger cousin Jian told others: "This boy at forty will naturally reach his grandfather's name and rank."

value.zh: 舉秀才，累遷太子舍人。
value.en: Recommended as Presented Scholar, he rose to Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
value.literal: He was recommended as Presented Scholar and was promoted in succession to Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

value.zh: 以父宦不通，弱年便欲紹興家業，啟齊武帝求自試，遷秘書丞。
value.en: His father's career had stalled; while still young Rong sought to revive the family fortunes, petitioned Emperor Wu of Qi for a trial appointment, and was made Secretary.
value.literal: Because his father's official career had not prospered, in weak years he wished to revive the family estate; he memorialized Emperor Wu of Qi asking to prove himself and was transferred to Secretary.

value.zh: 從叔儉初有儀同之授，贈儉詩及書，儉甚奇之，笑謂人曰：「穰侯印詎便可解。」
value.en: When his cousin Jian first received appointment as Equal to the Three Excellencies, Rong sent him a poem and letter; Jian was astonished and smiled: "So the seal of Ranghou can be handed over already?"
value.literal: When his father's younger cousin Jian first received appointment as Equal to the Three Excellencies, Rong sent him a poem and letter; Jian marveled greatly and smiling told others: "Can the seal of Ranghou really be taken off so soon?"

value.zh: 曆丹陽丞，中書郎。
value.en: He served as Assistant Magistrate of Danyang and Gentleman of the Secretariat.
value.literal: He served as Assistant Magistrate of Danyang and Gentleman of the Secretariat.

value.zh: 永明末，武帝欲北侵，使毛惠秀畫漢武北伐圖，融因此上疏，開張北侵之議。
value.en: At the end of Yongming, when Emperor Wu planned a northern campaign and had Mao Huixiu paint Han Wudi's northern expedition, Rong submitted a memorial urging invasion.
value.literal: At the end of the Yongming era Emperor Wu wished to invade the north and had Mao Huixiu paint Emperor Wu of Han's northern campaign; Rong therefore submitted a memorial opening discussion of northern invasion.

value.zh: 圖成，上置琅邪城射堂壁上，遊幸輒觀焉。
value.en: When the painting was finished the emperor hung it in the archery hall at Langya city and viewed it on every visit.
value.literal: When the painting was finished the emperor placed it on the wall of the archery hall at Langya city and viewed it whenever he toured.

value.zh: 九年，芳林園禊宴，使融為曲水詩序，當時稱之。
value.en: In the ninth year, at the Fanglin Garden spring purification, he had Rong write the preface to the winding-water poems; contemporaries praised it.
value.literal: In the ninth year, at the Fanglin Garden spring purification feast, he had Rong compose the preface to the winding-water poems; men of the time praised it.

value.zh: 上以融才辯，使兼主客，接魏使房景高、宋弁。
value.en: The emperor, noting Rong's eloquence, also made him Chief of Guests to receive the Wei envoys Fang Jinggao and Song Bian.
value.literal: The emperor, because Rong was talented and eloquent, had him additionally serve as Chief of Guests and receive the Wei envoys Fang Jinggao and Song Bian.

value.zh: 弁見融年少，問：「主客年幾？」
value.en: Bian saw that Rong was young and asked: "How old is the Chief of Guests?"
value.literal: Bian saw Rong was young and asked: "How old is the Chief of Guests?"

value.zh: 融曰：「五十之年，久踰其半。」
value.en: Rong replied: "Fifty years—well past the halfway mark."
value.literal: Rong said: "Of fifty years, long past the half."

value.zh: 景高又云：「在北聞主客曲水詩序勝延年，實願一見。」
value.en: Jinggao added: "In the north I heard your winding-water preface surpasses Yannian's—I long to see it."
value.literal: Jinggao also said: "In the north I heard the Chief of Guests' preface to the winding-water poems surpasses Yannian; I truly wish to see it."

value.zh: 融乃示之。
value.en: Rong showed it to them.
value.literal: Rong then showed it.

value.zh: 後日，宋弁於瑤池堂謂融曰：「昔觀相如封禪，以知漢武之德，今覽王生詩序，用見齊主之盛。」
value.en: Later at Yaochi Hall Song Bian told Rong: "Reading Sima Xiangru's feng-shan text revealed Han Wudi's virtue; reading Master Wang's preface reveals our lord's splendor."
value.literal: Later, Song Bian at Yaochi Hall said to Rong: "Once reading Sima Xiangru's feng and shan text, one knew the virtue of Han Wu; now reading Master Wang's poem preface, one sees the splendor of the Qi lord."

value.zh: 融曰：「皇家盛明，豈直比蹤漢武，更慚鄙制，無以遠匹相如。」
value.en: Rong replied: "Our dynasty's brilliance far exceeds Han Wudi's; my humble piece cannot compare with Xiangru."
value.literal: Rong said: "Our house's brilliance—how could it merely follow Han Wu? I am all the more ashamed of my crude composition; it cannot remotely match Xiangru."

value.zh: 上以魏所送馬不稱，使融問之曰：「秦西冀北，實多駿驥，而魏之良馬，乃駑不若，將旦旦信誓，有時而爽，駉駉之牧，遂不能嗣？」
value.en: Because the horses Wei sent were poor, the emperor had Rong ask: "Qin west and Ji north abound in fine steeds, yet Wei's gifts are nags—has sworn faith broken, and the pastures failed?"
value.literal: The emperor, because the horses Wei sent were unworthy, had Rong ask: "West of Qin and north of Ji truly have many fine steeds, yet Wei's good horses are inferior nags—is the daily sworn faith sometimes broken, and the pastures of spirited horses no longer bred?"

value.zh: 宋弁曰：「當是不習地土。」
value.en: Song Bian said: "Perhaps they are unused to the soil here."
value.literal: Song Bian said: "Perhaps they are unused to the soil."

value.zh: 融曰：「周穆馬跡遍於天下，若騏騮之性，因地而遷，則造父之策，有時而躓。」
value.en: Rong said: "King Mu's horses ranged the world; if fine breeds change with soil, then Zaofu's art would sometimes fail."
value.literal: Rong said: "King Mu of Zhou's horses' tracks covered the world; if the nature of qiji and juli shifts with land, then Zaofu's methods would sometimes stumble."

value.zh: 弁曰：「王主客何為勤勤於千里？」
value.en: Bian asked: "Why is the Chief of Guests so eager for horses from a thousand li away?"
value.literal: Bian said: "Why is the Chief of Guests so earnest about a thousand li?"

value.zh: 融曰：「卿國既異其優劣，聊復相訪，若千里斯至，聖上當駕鼓車。」
value.en: Rong said: "Since your state disputes their quality, I ask again—if they truly come from afar, our emperor will drive the drum carriage to meet them."
value.literal: Rong said: "Since your state differs on quality, I merely inquire again; if they arrive from a thousand li, the sage emperor will drive the drum carriage."

value.zh: 弁曰：「向意既須，必不能駕鼓車也。」
value.en: Bian said: "If you truly need them, you surely will not send the drum carriage."
value.literal: Bian said: "Since the intent is need, they surely cannot drive the drum carriage."

value.zh: 融曰：「買死馬之骨，亦以郭隗之故。」
value.en: Rong said: "Even buying dead horses' bones honors Guo Kui's memory."
value.literal: Rong said: "Buying the bones of dead horses is also for Guo Kui's sake."

value.zh: 弁不能答。
value.en: Bian had no reply.
value.literal: Bian could not answer.

value.zh: 融躁于名利，自恃人地，三十內望為公輔。
value.en: Rong hungered for fame and office; trusting in birth and rank, before thirty he expected the highest posts.
value.literal: Rong was impatient for fame and profit; relying on his birth and station, before thirty he looked to become chief minister and assistant.

value.zh: 初為司徒法曹，詣王僧佑，因遇沈昭略，未相識。
value.en: Early in his career, as Law Clerk of the Minister of Education, he called on Wang Sengyou and met Shen Zhaolüe, a stranger to him.
value.literal: At first as Law Clerk of the Minister of Education he called on Wang Sengyou and chanced to meet Shen Zhaolüe, whom he did not know.

value.zh: 昭略屢顧盼，謂主人曰：「是何年少？」
value.en: Zhaolüe glanced back again and again and asked the host: "Who is this young man?"
value.literal: Zhaolüe looked back repeatedly and said to the host: "What youth is this?"

value.zh: 融殊不平，謂曰：「僕出於扶桑，入于湯穀，照耀天下，誰雲不知，而卿此問？」
value.en: Rong was furious: "I rise from Fusang and set in Tanggu, shining over the world—who does not know me, that you should ask?"
value.literal: Rong was greatly displeased and said: "I come from Fusang and enter Tanggu, shining on all under heaven—who says they do not know, yet you ask this?"

value.zh: 昭略云：「不知許事，且食蛤蜊。」
value.en: Zhaolüe said: "I know nothing of that—let us eat clams instead."
value.literal: Zhaolüe said: "I know nothing of such things—let us eat clams."

value.zh: 融曰：「物以群分，方以類聚，君長東隅，居然應嗜此族。」
value.en: Rong retorted: "Things flock by kind and regions by class—you rule the eastern corner and naturally favor this tribe."
value.literal: Rong said: "Things group by kind, regions by class—you preside over the eastern corner and naturally should love this tribe."

value.zh: 其高自標置如此。
value.en: Such was his towering self-regard.
value.literal: Such was his lofty self-regard.

value.zh: 及魏軍動，竟陵王子良于東府募人，板融甯朔將軍、軍主。
value.en: When Wei armies mobilized, the Prince of Jingling Ziliang recruited at the Eastern Mansion and appointed Rong General Who Pacifies the North and Army Commander.
value.literal: When Wei troops moved, the Prince of Jingling Ziliang at the Eastern Mansion recruited men and appointed Rong General Who Pacifies the North and Army Commander.

value.zh: 融文辭捷速，有所造作，援筆可待，子良特相友好。
value.en: Rong wrote with swift grace; whatever he undertook he finished at a stroke; Ziliang favored him especially.
value.literal: Rong's literary phrasing was quick; whatever he wrote he could finish at the brush; Ziliang was especially friendly with him.

value.zh: 晚節大習騎馬，招集江西傖楚數百人，並有幹用，融特為謀主。
value.en: In his later years he took hard to horsemanship, gathered several hundred tough men from west of the river and Chu, all useful fighters, and made himself their chief strategist.
value.literal: In late years he greatly practiced horsemanship, gathered several hundred rough men of Jiang west and Chu, all capable, and Rong alone was their chief planner.

value.zh: 武帝病篤暫絕，子良在殿內，太孫未入，融戎服絳衫，於中書省合口斷東宮仗不得進，欲矯詔立子良。
value.en: When Emperor Wu lay gravely ill and briefly lost consciousness, Ziliang remained in the palace while the heir had not entered; Rong in martial dress and scarlet shirt blocked the Eastern Palace guard at the Secretariat gate, intending to forge an edict and install Ziliang.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu was gravely ill and briefly lost consciousness, Ziliang was in the palace hall and the heir had not entered; Rong in martial dress and scarlet shirt blocked the Eastern Palace guard at the Secretariat gate from entering, wishing to forge an edict and install Ziliang.

value.zh: 詔草已立，上重蘇，朝事委西昌侯鸞。
value.en: The draft edict was already written; the emperor rallied and entrusted affairs to the Marquis of Xichang Luan.
value.literal: The draft edict was already written; the emperor recovered and court affairs were entrusted to the Marquis of Xichang Luan.

value.zh: 梁武謂範雲曰：「左手據天下圖，右手刎其喉，愚夫不為。
value.en: Emperor Wu of Liang told Fan Yun: "Left hand on the empire's map, right hand at its throat—no fool would do that.
value.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang said to Fan Yun: "Left hand holding the map of all under heaven, right hand cutting its throat—no fool would do that.

value.zh: 主上大漸，國家自有故事，道路籍籍，將有非常之舉，卿聞之乎？」
value.en: The emperor is failing; the state has its own precedents; the roads buzz with talk of something extraordinary—have you heard?"
value.literal: The lord is failing; the state has its own precedents; on the roads there is clamor that something extraordinary will happen—have you heard?"

value.zh: 雲不敢答。
value.en: Yun dared not answer.
value.literal: Yun did not dare answer.

value.zh: 俄而帝崩，融乃處分以子良兵禁諸門，西昌侯聞，急馳到雲龍門，不得進，乃曰：「有敕召我。」
value.en: Soon the emperor died; Rong deployed Ziliang's troops to seal the gates; the Marquis of Xichang galloped to Cloud Dragon Gate but could not enter and cried: "An edict summons me."
value.literal: Soon the emperor died; Rong then disposed troops with Ziliang's soldiers to seal the gates; the Marquis of Xichang heard and galloped to Cloud Dragon Gate but could not enter; he then said: "There is an edict summoning me."

value.zh: 仍排而入，奉太孫登殿，命左右扶出子良，指麾音響如鍾，殿內無不從命。
value.en: He forced his way in, escorted the heir to the throne, ordered attendants to lead Ziliang out; his commands rang like a bell and none in the hall disobeyed.
value.literal: He pushed in, escorted the heir to the throne, ordered attendants to lead Ziliang out; his commands rang like a bell and none in the hall disobeyed.

value.zh: 融知不遂，乃釋服還省，歎曰：「公誤我。」
value.en: Knowing he had failed, Rong changed out of martial dress, returned to his office, and sighed: "The duke misled me."
value.literal: Rong knew he would not succeed, put off his martial dress and returned to his office, and sighed: "The duke misled me."

value.zh: 郁林深怨融，即位十餘日，收下廷尉獄。
value.en: Emperor Yulin deeply hated Rong; within ten days of enthronement he seized him and cast him into the Court of Justice.
value.literal: Emperor Yulin deeply resented Rong; more than ten days after taking the throne he seized him and put him in the Court of Justice prison.

value.zh: 使中丞孔珪倚為奏曰：「融姿性剛險，立身浮競，動跡驚群，抗言異類。
value.en: He had Censor Kong Gui draft the impeachment: "Rong's nature is harsh and treacherous, his conduct restless and ambitious; his deeds startle the crowd and his words defy convention.
value.literal: He had the Censor Kong Gui draft the memorial on his behalf: "Rong's nature is hard and dangerous, his conduct floating and competitive; his movements startle the crowd and his bold words differ from the kind.

value.zh: 近塞外微塵，苦求將領，遂招納不逞，扇誘荒傖。
value.en: Lately, with dust on the frontier, he bitterly sought command and recruited unruly men, stirring up wild northerners.
value.literal: Lately at the frontier dust he bitterly sought command and thus recruited unruly men, inciting wild northerners.

value.zh: 狡弄威聲，專行權利，反復唇齒之間，傾動頰舌之內，威福自己，無所忌憚，誹謗朝政，曆毀王公。
value.en: He played at intimidation, grasped power for himself, whispered and shouted as he pleased, feared nothing, slandered the court, and repeatedly defamed princes and nobles.
value.literal: Cunningly wielding threatening voice, exclusively exercising power and profit, back and forth between lips and teeth, shaking within cheek and tongue, authority and favor from himself, without dread; slandering court governance, repeatedly destroying kings and dukes.

value.zh: 謂己才流，無所推下，事暴遠近，使融依源據答。」
value.en: He claimed no man matched his talent and birth; the charges were known far and wide; let Rong answer point by point."
value.literal: He said his talent and class had none beneath him; the matter was exposed far and near; let Rong answer according to source and evidence."

value.zh: 融辭曰：「囚實頑蔽，觸行多愆。
value.en: Rong replied: "The prisoner is indeed dull and erring; his conduct has many faults.
value.literal: Rong replied: "The prisoner is indeed stubborn and blind; his conduct has many faults.

value.zh: 但夙忝門素，得奉教君子。
value.en: Yet from youth I have borne my family's name and received instruction from gentlemen.
value.literal: Yet from old I have disgraced my gate and lineage by receiving instruction from gentlemen.

value.zh: 爰自總發，迄將立年，州閭鄉党，見許愚慎。
value.en: From boyhood until nearly adulthood, neighbors in district and village called me prudent.
value.literal: From first tying the hair until nearly the age of standing, in district and village my neighbors called me cautious.

value.zh: 過蒙大行皇帝獎育之恩，又荷文皇帝識擢之重，司徒公賜預士林，安陸王曲垂盼接，前後陳伐虜之計，亦仰簡先朝。
value.en: I enjoyed the late Grand Emperor's nurturing favor and the late Literary Emperor's recognition; the Minister of Education admitted me to the literati, the Prince of Anlu favored me; my plans against the northern foe were also approved by the former court.
value.literal: I overly received the late Grand Emperor's nurturing favor and also bore the late Literary Emperor's recognition and promotion; the Minister of Education granted me place among the literati, the Prince of Anlu graciously received me; my plans for campaigning against the barbarians were also approved by the former court.

value.zh: 今段犬羊乍擾，令囚草撰符詔。
value.en: When the northern barbarians suddenly stirred, I was ordered to draft edicts and warrants.
value.literal: Now when the dogs and sheep suddenly stirred, the prisoner was ordered to draft edicts and warrants.

value.zh: 及司徒宣敕招募，同例非一，實以戎事不小，不敢承教。
value.en: The Minister of Education again proclaimed recruitment; others did the same—it was not because the war was minor that I refused.
value.literal: Again the Minister of Education proclaimed orders to recruit; there were many like cases—not because military matters were small did I dare refuse instruction.

value.zh: 續蒙軍號，賜使招集，銜敕而行，非敢虛扇。
value.en: I received a military title and orders to gather troops; I carried out the command—I did not stir empty alarm.
value.literal: I again received a military title and was granted orders to gather men; I carried the command and went—not daring to stir empty alarm.

value.zh: 且張弄威聲，應有形跡。
value.en: As for playing at intimidation, there should be visible evidence.
value.literal: Moreover, cunningly wielding threatening voice should have visible traces.

value.zh: 專行權利，又無贓賄。
value.en: Grasping power for profit—again, there is no bribe.
value.literal: Exclusively exercising power and profit—again there is no bribe.

value.zh: 反復唇齒之間，未審悉與誰言？
value.en: Whispering between lips and teeth—with whom was all this spoken?
value.literal: Back and forth between lips and teeth—I do not know with whom all this was spoken?

value.zh: 傾動頰舌之內，不容都無主此。
value.en: Shouting within cheek and tongue—surely someone must have presided over it?
value.literal: Shaking within cheek and tongue—surely there cannot be no one who presided over this?

value.zh: 自上甘露頌及銀甕啟、三日詩序、接虜使語辭，竭思稱揚，得非誹謗。
value.en: From the Sweet Dew hymn to the silver-jar memorial, the three-day poem preface, and my words with barbarian envoys—I exhausted myself in praise; how is that slander?
value.literal: From the Sweet Dew hymn upward, the silver-jar memorial, the three-day poem preface, and the words receiving the barbarian envoys—I exhausted thought in praise; how can this be slander?

value.zh: 囚才分本劣，謬被策用，悚怍之情，夙宵兢惕，自循自省，並愧流言。
value.en: My talent is by nature modest; wrongly placed in office, I tremble day and night; examining myself, I am ashamed before gossip.
value.literal: The prisoner's talent and measure are by nature inferior; wrongly chosen for use, my fearful shame day and night is vigilant; examining myself, I am ashamed before idle talk.

value.zh: 伏惟明皇臨宇，普天蒙澤，戊寅赦恩，輕重必宥，百日曠期，始蒙旬日，一介罪身，獨嬰憲劾。」
value.en: I bow before the bright emperor whose grace covers the realm; the Wuyin amnesty spares light and heavy alike, and within the hundred-day grace I had barely ten days—a lone guilty man alone bears punishment."
value.literal: I bow that the bright emperor overlooks the realm and all heaven receives grace; the Wuyin amnesty must spare light and heavy alike, and the hundred-day grace period had only just granted ten days—a lone guilty body alone bears punishment."

value.zh: 融被收，朋友部曲，參問北寺，相繼於道；
value.en: When Rong was seized, friends and retainers lined the road to North Temple to inquire after him;
value.literal: When Rong was seized, friends and retainers came to inquire at North Temple one after another on the road;

value.zh: 請救於子良，子良不敢救；
value.en: they begged Ziliang to save him, but Ziliang dared not;
value.literal: they asked Ziliang for rescue, and Ziliang did not dare rescue;

value.zh: 西昌侯固爭不得。
value.en: the Marquis of Xichang argued fiercely but could not prevail.
value.literal: the Marquis of Xichang argued hard but could not prevail.

value.zh: 詔于獄賜死，時年二十七。
value.en: An edict ordered death in prison; he was twenty-seven.
value.literal: An edict granted death in prison; he was then twenty-seven.

value.zh: 臨死歎曰：「我若不為百歲老母，當吐一言。」
value.en: Facing death he sighed: "Were it not for my aged mother, I would speak one word."
value.literal: Facing death he sighed: "If not for my hundred-year-old mother, I would speak one word."

value.zh: 融意欲指斥帝在東宮時過失也。
value.en: Rong meant to expose the emperor's misconduct from his days as heir.
value.literal: Rong intended to denounce the emperor's faults when he was Eastern Palace heir.

value.zh: 先是，太學生會稽魏准，以才學為融所賞，既欲奉子良，而准鼓成其事。
value.en: Earlier Wei Zhun of Kuaiji, a Grand Academy student admired by Rong for talent, wished to support Ziliang and pressed the plot forward.
value.literal: Earlier, Wei Zhun of Kuaiji, a Grand Academy student, was admired by Rong for talent and learning; wishing to support Ziliang, Zhun urged the matter on.

value.zh: 太學生虞羲、丘國賓竊相謂曰：「竟陵才弱，王中書無斷，敗在眼中矣。」
value.en: Grand Academy students Yu Xi and Qiu Guobin whispered: "Jingling's talent is weak and Wang the Secretariat Director lacks resolve—defeat is plain to see."
value.literal: Grand Academy students Yu Xi and Qiu Guobin whispered to each other: "The Prince of Jingling's talent is weak and Director of the Secretariat Wang lacks resolve—defeat is before our eyes."

value.zh: 及融誅，召准入舍人省詰問，遂懼而死，舉體皆青，時人以准膽破。
value.en: When Rong was executed, Zhun was summoned to the Attendants' Office for questioning; terror killed him—his whole body turned blue—and men said his gall had burst.
value.literal: When Rong was executed, Zhun was summoned to the Attendants' Office for questioning; in fear he died, his whole body turning blue; men of the time said Zhun's gall had burst.

value.zh: 融文集行于時。
value.en: Rong's collected writings circulated in his day.
value.literal: Rong's collected writings circulated in his time.

value.zh: 列傳第二十九
value.en: the twenty-ninth year of Biography
value.literal: Biographies 29

value.zh: 孝綽字孝綽，本名冉。
value.en: Liu Xiaochuo, courtesy name Xiaochuo, had the original given name Ran.
value.literal: Xiaochuo, courtesy name Xiaochuo, original given name Ran.

value.zh: 幼聰敏，七歲能屬文。
value.en: From childhood he was clever; at seven he could compose prose.
value.literal: From childhood he was clever; at seven he could compose prose.

value.zh: 舅齊中書郎王融深賞異之，與同載以適親友，號曰神童。
value.en: His uncle Wang Rong, Secretariat Gentleman of Qi, greatly admired him, took him in the same carriage to visit kin and friends, and called him a divine child.
value.literal: His uncle Wang Rong, Secretariat Gentleman of Qi, greatly admired and favored him, took him in the same carriage to visit kin and friends, and called him a divine child.

value.zh: 融每曰：「天下文章若無我，當歸阿士。」
value.en: Rong often said: "If there were no me in the world's literature, it would belong to A Shi."
value.literal: Rong often said: "If there were no me in the world's literature, it would belong to A Shi."

value.zh: 阿士即孝綽小字也。
value.en: A Shi was Xiaochuo's childhood name.
value.literal: A Shi was Xiaochuo's childhood name.

value.zh: 父繪，齊時掌詔誥，孝綽時年十四，繪常使代草之。
value.en: His father Hui in Qi times controlled edicts and patents; when Xiaochuo was fourteen, Hui often had him draft them in his place.
value.literal: His father Hui in Qi times was in charge of edicts and patents; when Xiaochuo was fourteen, Hui often had him draft them.

value.zh: 父党沈約、任昉、范雲等聞其名，命駕造焉，昉尤相賞好。
value.en: Shen Yue, Ren Fang, Fan Yun, and other friends of his father heard his name and came to visit; Fang especially prized and befriended him.
value.literal: Shen Yue, Ren Fang, Fan Yun, and other friends of his father heard his name and ordered their carriages to visit him; Fang especially prized and befriended him.

value.zh: 範雲年長繪十餘歲，其子孝才與孝綽年並十四五。
value.en: Fan Yun was more than ten years older than Hui; his son Xiaocai and Xiaochuo were both fourteen or fifteen.
value.literal: Fan Yun was more than ten years older than Hui; his son Xiaocai and Xiaochuo were both fourteen or fifteen.

value.zh: 及雲遇孝綽，便申伯季，乃命孝才拜之。
value.en: When Yun met Xiaochuo, he declared elder and younger brotherhood and ordered Xiaocai to bow to him.
value.literal: When Yun met Xiaochuo, he declared elder and younger brotherhood and ordered Xiaocai to bow to him.

value.zh: 兼善草隸，自以書似父，乃變為別體。
value.en: He was also skilled in cursive and clerical script; thinking his writing resembled his father's, he changed to a different style.
value.literal: He was also skilled in cursive and clerical script; thinking his writing resembled his father's, he changed to a different style.

value.zh: 李安人
value.en: Li Anren
value.literal: Li Anren

value.zh: 祖嶷，衛軍將軍。
value.en: His grandfather Yi served as General of the Guards.
value.literal: His grandfather Yi was General of the Guards.

value.zh: 父欽之，薛令。
value.en: His father Qinzhi served as magistrate of Xue.
value.literal: His father Qinzhi was magistrate of Xue.

value.zh: 子元履，幼有操業，甚閑政體，為司徒竟陵王子良法曹參軍。
value.en: His son Yuanlü showed discipline from boyhood and a keen grasp of government procedure; he served as Legal Bureau Attendant to Prince Ziliang of Jingling, the Heir Apparent.
value.literal: His son Yuanlü, from childhood possessed moral conduct and was thoroughly versed in administrative forms; he served as Legal Bureau Attendant to the Prince of Jingling, the Heir Apparent.

value.zh: 與王融遊狎，及王融誅，郁林敕元履隨右衛將軍王廣之北征，密令於北殺之。
value.en: He was intimate with Wang Rong; after Wang Rong's execution, Emperor Yulin ordered Yuanlü to accompany Right Guard General Wang Guangzhi northward, secretly commanding that he be killed on the road.
value.literal: He associated closely with Wang Rong; when Wang Rong was executed, Emperor Yulin ordered Yuanlü to follow the Right Guard General Wang Guangzhi on the northern campaign, secretly instructing him to kill Yuanlü in the north.

value.zh: 廣之先為安人所厚，又知元履無過，甚擁護之。
value.en: Wang Guangzhi had once owed much to Li Anren and knew Yuanlü was innocent, so he shielded him with all his might.
value.literal: Guangzhi had earlier been greatly favored by Anren and knew Yuanlü was guiltless, so he protected him zealously.

value.zh: 會郁林敗死，元履拜謝廣之，曰：「二十二載，父母之年，自此以外，丈人之賜也。」
value.en: When Emperor Yulin met his downfall, Yuanlü thanked Wang Guangzhi and said, "Twenty-two years—the span my parents might have wished for me; anything beyond that I owe to you, sir."
value.literal: When Emperor Yulin fell and died, Yuanlü bowed in thanks to Guangzhi and said, "Twenty-two years—the years of my parents; beyond that, it is the gift of my elder."

value.zh: 仕梁為吳郡太守，度支尚書，衡、廣、青、冀四州刺史。
value.en: Under Liang he rose to Administrator of Wu commandery, Minister of Revenue, and Inspector of Heng, Guang, Qing, and Ji provinces.
value.literal: He served Liang as Administrator of Wu commandery, Minister of Revenue, and Inspector of the four provinces Heng, Guang, Qing, and Ji.

value.zh: 列傳第四十九
value.en: Biography Forty-Nine
value.literal: Biography 49

value.zh: 後為司徒竟陵王記室參軍。
value.en: Later he served as recorder-aide to the Minister of Education, Prince Jingling.
value.literal: Later he served as recorder-aide to the Minister of Education, Prince Jingling.

value.zh: 時琅邪王融有才俊，自謂無對當時，見昉之文，怳然自失。
value.en: At that time Wang Rong of Langya had literary talent and brilliance and considered himself without rival in the age. When he saw Fang's writings he was suddenly lost to himself.
value.literal: At that time Wang Rong of Langya had literary talent and brilliance; he considered himself without rival in the age; when he saw Fang's writings he was suddenly lost to himself.

value.zh: 以父喪去官，泣血三年，杖而後起。
value.en: On his father's death he left office. He wept blood for three years and only rose with a staff.
value.literal: On his father's death he left office; he wept blood for three years and only rose with a staff.

value.zh: 齊武帝謂昉伯遐曰：「聞昉哀瘠過禮，使人憂之，非直亡卿之寶，亦時才可惜。
value.en: Emperor Wu of Qi told Fang's elder uncle Xia, "I hear Fang's mourning emaciation exceeds the rites and causes worry. It is not only the loss of your treasure but also a pity for the talent of the age.
value.literal: Emperor Wu of Qi said to Fang's elder uncle Xia, "I hear Fang's mourning emaciation exceeds the rites and causes one worry; it is not only the loss of your treasure but also a pity for the talent of the age.

value.zh: 宜深相全譬。」
value.en: You should deeply comfort and instruct him."
value.literal: You should deeply comfort and instruct him."

value.zh: 遐使進飲食，當時勉勵，回即歐出。
value.en: Xia had food and drink brought in and urged him on, but as soon as he returned Fang vomited it out.
value.literal: Xia had food and drink brought in and at the time urged him on, but as soon as he returned he vomited it out.

value.zh: 昉父遙本性重檳榔，以為常餌，臨終嘗求之，剖百許口，不得好者，昉亦所嗜好，深以為恨，遂終身不嚐檳榔。
value.en: Fang's father Yao prized betel nut as a regular food. On his deathbed he once asked for it, but of a hundred or so split open none was good. Fang too was fond of it and deeply regretted this, and never tasted betel nut for the rest of his life.
value.literal: Fang's father Yao by nature prized betel nut as a regular food; on his deathbed he once asked for it; they split open a hundred or so, but could not find a good one; Fang too was fond of it and deeply regretted this, and therefore never tasted betel nut for his whole life.

value.zh: 遭繼母憂，昉先以毀瘠，每一慟絕，良久乃蘇，因廬於墓側，以終喪禮。
value.en: When he met with mourning for his stepmother, Fang had already been emaciated by grief. Each time he wailed he fainted and only after a long while revived. He built a hut by the tomb and completed the mourning rites there.
value.literal: When he met with mourning for his stepmother, Fang had already been emaciated by grief; each time he wailed he fainted and only after a long while revived; he therefore built a hut by the tomb and completed the mourning rites there.

value.zh: 哭泣之地，草為不生。
value.en: At the place of his weeping the grass would not grow.
value.literal: At the place of his weeping the grass did not grow.

value.zh: 昉素強壯，腰帶甚充，服闋後不復可識。
value.en: Fang had always been robust and his waist belt very full. After the mourning period ended he could no longer be recognized.
value.literal: Fang had always been robust; his waist belt was very full; after the mourning period ended he could no longer be recognized.

value.zh: 列傳第五十
value.en: the 50th year of Biographies
value.literal: Biographies, number fifty.

value.zh: 休源十一而孤，居喪盡禮，每見父手所寫書，必哀慟流涕不能自勝，見者莫不為之垂泣。
value.en: Xiuyuan was orphaned at eleven and observed the mourning rites with complete devotion. Whenever he saw books written in his father's hand, he would weep uncontrollably, and those who witnessed his grief wept with him.
value.literal: Xiuyuan was orphaned at eleven; he observed mourning to the full rites. Whenever he saw books written in his father's hand, he would mourn and weep beyond control; those who saw it all wept for him.

value.zh: 後就吳興沈麟士受經，略通大義。
value.en: He later studied the classics under Shen Linshi of Wuxing and gained a general understanding of their essential meaning.
value.literal: Later he studied the classics under Shen Linshi of Wuxing and gained a general grasp of their essential meaning.

value.zh: 州舉秀才，太尉徐孝嗣省其策，深善之，謂同坐曰：「董仲舒、華令思何以尚此，可謂後生之准的也。
value.en: The province recommended him as a cultivated talent. Grand Commandant Xu Xiaosi examined his examination answer and was deeply impressed, saying to those present, "How could Dong Zhongshu or Hua Lingsi surpass this? He is a standard by which later generations may be measured.
value.literal: The province recommended him as a cultivated talent. Grand Commandant Xu Xiaosi examined his examination answer and deeply approved it, saying to those seated with him: "How could Dong Zhongshu or Hua Lingsi surpass this? He may be called the target for later generations.

value.zh: 觀此足稱王佐之才。」
value.en: From this one can see that he truly possesses the talent of a chief minister."
value.literal: Judging from this, he fully deserves to be called talent for assisting a king."

value.zh: 琅邪王融雅相友善，乃薦之于司徒竟陵王，為西邸學士。
value.en: Wang Rong of Langya became his close friend and recommended him to Prince Jingling, Minister of Works, who appointed him a scholar of the Western Lodge.
value.literal: Wang Rong of Langya was elegantly friendly with him and recommended him to Prince Jingling, Minister of Works, as a scholar of the Western Lodge.

value.zh: 革幼而聰敏，早有才思，六歲便解屬文。
value.en: Ge was intelligent from childhood and showed early literary talent; at the age of six he could already compose prose.
value.literal: Ge from youth was intelligent and keen; early he had literary talent, and at six he could already compose prose.

value.zh: 柔之深加賞器，曰：「此兒必興吾門。」
value.en: Rouzhi admired him deeply, saying, "This boy will surely bring honor to our house."
value.literal: Rouzhi deeply admired him, saying: "This child will surely raise up our house."

value.zh: 九歲丁父艱，與第四弟觀同生，少孤貧，傍無師友，兄弟自相訓勖，讀書精力不倦。
value.en: At nine he entered mourning for his father. He and his fourth younger brother Guan, born of the same mother, were orphaned young and poor, with no teachers or friends nearby. The brothers encouraged each other in study and read with tireless energy.
value.literal: At nine he entered mourning for his father. He and his fourth younger brother Guan were born of the same mother; orphaned young and poor, with no teachers or friends nearby, the brothers encouraged each other in study, reading with tireless energy.

value.zh: 十六喪母，以孝聞。
value.en: When his mother died at sixteen, he became renowned for his filial devotion.
value.literal: At sixteen his mother died; he became known for filial piety.

value.zh: 服闋，與觀俱詣太學，補國子生，舉高第。
value.en: When mourning ended, he and Guan both entered the Imperial University as students of the National University and were recommended with the highest marks.
value.literal: When mourning ended, he and Guan both went to the Imperial University, were enrolled as students of the National University, and were recommended with highest marks.

value.zh: 齊中書郎王融、吏部郎謝朓雅相欽重。
value.en: Wang Rong, Director of the Secretariat under Qi, and Xie Tiao, Director of the Personnel Bureau, both deeply admired and esteemed him.
value.literal: Wang Rong, Director of the Secretariat under Qi, and Xie Tiao, Director of the Personnel Bureau, both deeply admired and esteemed him.

value.zh: 朓嘗行還過候革，時大寒雪，見革弊絮單席，而耽學不倦，嗟歎久之，乃脫其所著襦，並手割半氈與革充臥具而去。
value.en: Tiao once returned from a journey and stopped to visit Ge. It was bitterly cold and snowing; he found Ge in worn cotton clothing on a single mat, yet still devoted to study without rest. Tiao sighed at length, then took off his own padded jacket and cut half a felt rug by hand to serve as Ge's bedding before departing.
value.literal: Tiao once returned from a journey and stopped to visit Ge. It was bitterly cold with snow; he saw Ge in worn cotton and on a single mat, yet devoted to study without weariness. Tiao sighed long, then took off his own padded jacket and with his own hands cut half a felt rug to serve as Ge's bedding before departing.

value.zh: 司徒竟陵王聞其名，引為西邸學士。
value.en: Prince Jingling, Minister of Works, heard of him and recruited him as a scholar of the Western Lodge.
value.literal: Prince Jingling, Minister of Works, heard his name and recruited him as a scholar of the Western Lodge.

value.zh: 弱冠舉南徐州秀才。
value.en: At his capping he was recommended as a cultivated talent of South Xuzhou.
value.literal: At his capping he was recommended as a cultivated talent of South Xuzhou.

value.zh: 時豫章胡諧之行州事，王融與諧之書令薦革。
value.en: At the time Hu Xiezhi of Yuzhang was acting in provincial affairs. Wang Rong wrote to Xiezhi instructing him to recommend Ge.
value.literal: At the time Hu Xiezhi of Yuzhang was acting in provincial affairs; Wang Rong wrote to Xiezhi instructing him to recommend Ge.

value.zh: 諧之方貢琅邪王泛，便以革代之。
value.en: Xiezhi had just presented Wang Fan of Langya as tribute and therefore substituted Ge in his place.
value.literal: Xiezhi had just presented Wang Fan of Langya as tribute and therefore replaced him with Ge.

value.zh: 僕射江祏深相引接，祏為太子詹事，啟革為丞。
value.en: Vice Director Jiang Si received him warmly. When Si became Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household, he recommended Ge as assistant.
value.literal: Vice Director Jiang Si deeply received and welcomed him. When Si became Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household, he recommended Ge as assistant.

value.zh: 祏時權傾朝右，以革才堪經國，令參掌機務，詔誥文檄皆委以具。
value.en: At the time Si wielded enormous power at court. Considering Ge's talent fit for governing the state, he had him take part in managing secret affairs. Edicts, proclamations, and dispatches were all entrusted to Ge to draft.
value.literal: At the time Si's power tilted the right side of the court; considering Ge's talent fit for governing the state, he had him take part in managing secret affairs. Edicts, proclamations, and dispatches were all entrusted to Ge to draft.

value.zh: 革防杜形跡，外人不知。
value.en: Ge kept his involvement concealed, and outsiders knew nothing of it.
value.literal: Ge guarded against revealing traces; outsiders did not know.

value.zh: 祏誅，賓客皆罹其罪，革獨以智免。
value.en: When Si was executed, his retainers all suffered for the crime, but Ge alone escaped through his shrewdness.
value.literal: When Si was executed, his retainers all suffered for the crime; Ge alone escaped through wisdom.

value.zh: 除尚書駕部郎。
value.en: He was appointed Director of the Chariot Bureau of the Imperial Secretariat.
value.literal: He was appointed Director of the Chariot Bureau of the Imperial Secretariat.

value.zh: 勉幼孤貧，早勵清節。
value.en: Mian was orphaned young and poor, and early cultivated purity of conduct.
value.literal: Mian was orphaned young and poor, and early cultivated purity of conduct.

value.zh: 年六歲，屬霖雨，家人祈霽，率爾為文，見稱耆宿。
value.en: At six, during prolonged rain, when the family prayed for clear skies, he spontaneously composed a text and was praised by elders.
value.literal: At six, during prolonged rain, when the family prayed for clear skies, he spontaneously composed a text and was praised by elders.

value.zh: 及長好學，宗人孝嗣見之歎曰：「此所謂人中之騏驥，必能致千里。」
value.en: When grown he loved learning. His clansman Xiaosi saw him and sighed, saying, "This is what they call a thoroughbred among men—he will surely reach a thousand li."
value.literal: When grown he loved learning. His clansman Xiaosi saw him and sighed, saying: "This is what they call a thoroughbred among men—he will surely reach a thousand li."

value.zh: 又嘗謂諸子曰：「此人師也，爾等則而行之。」
value.en: He also once told his sons, "This man is a teacher; you should take him as your model and follow him."
value.literal: He also once told his sons: "This man is a teacher; you should take him as your model and follow him."

value.zh: 年十八，召為國子生，便下帷專學，精力無怠。
value.en: At eighteen he was summoned as a student of the National University, drew the curtain and devoted himself to study, his energy never slackening.
value.literal: At eighteen he was summoned as a student of the National University, drew the curtain and devoted himself to study, his energy never slackening.

value.zh: 同時儕輩肅而敬之。
value.en: Contemporaries of the same generation were solemn and respectful toward him.
value.literal: Contemporaries of the same generation were solemn and respectful toward him.

value.zh: 祭酒王儉每見，常目送之，曰：「此子非常器也。」
value.en: Chancellor Wang Jian whenever he saw him would gaze after him and say, "This youth is no ordinary vessel."
value.literal: Chancellor Wang Jian whenever he saw him would gaze after him and say: "This youth is no ordinary vessel."

value.zh: 每稱有宰輔之量。
value.en: He often declared that Mian had the capacity of a chief minister.
value.literal: He often declared that Mian had the capacity of a chief minister.

value.zh: 射策甲科，起家王國侍郎，補太學博士。
value.en: In the archery-and-policy examination he ranked in the top class. He began his career as Gentleman of a princely domain and was appointed erudite of the Imperial University.
value.literal: In the archery-and-policy examination he ranked in the top class. He began his career as Gentleman of a princely domain and was appointed erudite of the Imperial University.

value.zh: 時每有議定，勉理證明允，莫能貶奪，同官咸取則焉。
value.en: Whenever there was deliberation and decision at the time, Mian's reasoning was clear and fair. None could diminish or overturn it, and colleagues all took him as their standard.
value.literal: Whenever there was deliberation and decision at the time, Mian's reasoning was clear and fair; none could diminish or overturn it, and colleagues all took him as their standard.

value.zh: 遷臨海王西中郎田曹行參軍，俄徙署都曹。
value.en: He was transferred to Acting Military Affairs Aide in the Field Bureau of the Western Palace Guard under Prince Linhai, and soon moved to serve in the Capital Bureau.
value.literal: He was transferred to Acting Military Affairs Aide in the Field Bureau of the Western Palace Guard under Prince Linhai, and soon moved to serve in the Capital Bureau.

value.zh: 時琅邪王融一時才俊，特相慕悅，嘗請交焉。
value.en: At the time Wang Rong of Langya was a leading talent of the age and especially admired him, once requesting friendship.
value.literal: At the time Wang Rong of Langya was a leading talent of the age and especially admired and delighted in him, once requesting friendship.

value.zh: 勉謂所親曰：「王郎名高望促，難可輕霹衣裾。」
value.en: Mian said to those close to him, "Master Wang's fame is high but his prospects are short; one cannot lightly attach oneself to his hem."
value.literal: Mian said to those close to him: "Master Wang's fame is high but his prospects are short; one cannot lightly attach oneself to his hem."

value.zh: 融後果陷於法，以此見推識鑒。
value.en: Rong later indeed fell afoul of the law; for this Mian was praised for his discernment.
value.literal: Rong later indeed fell afoul of the law; for this Mian was praised for his discernment.

value.zh: 累遷領軍長史。
value.en: He was repeatedly promoted to chief clerk of the Army of the Guard.
value.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to chief clerk of the Army of the Guard.

value.zh: 趙氏之先，與秦共祖。
value.en: The Zhao clan's forebears shared an ancestor with Qin.
value.literal: Zhao clan's forebears, together with Qin shared ancestor.

value.zh: 至中衍，為帝大戊御。
value.en: Reaching Zhong Yan, he was Emperor Da Wu's charioteer.
value.literal: Reached Zhong Yan, was Emperor Da Wu's charioteer.

value.zh: 其後世蜚廉有子二人，而命其一子曰惡來，事紂，為周所殺，其後為秦。
value.en: In his later generations, Feilian had two sons, and named one of them Elai. Elai served King Zhou and was killed by the Zhou. His descendants became Qin.
value.literal: His later generations Feilian had sons two, and named his one son said Elai, served Zhou, was by Zhou killed, his descendants became Qin.

value.zh: 惡來弟曰季勝，其後為趙。
value.en: Elai's younger brother was named Jisheng. His descendants became Zhao.
value.literal: Elai's younger brother named Jisheng, his descendants became Zhao.

value.zh: 王還，不聽秦，秦圍邯鄲。
value.en: The king returned to Handan and refused Qin's terms. Qin then laid siege to the capital.
value.literal: The king returned, did not heed Qin, Qin besieged Handan.

value.zh: 武垣令傅豹、王容、蘇射率燕眾反燕地。
value.en: The magistrate of Wuyuan, Fu Bao, along with Wang Rong and Su She, led the Yan garrison in a revolt and returned to Yan territory.
value.literal: The magistrate of Wuyuan, Fu Bao, Wang Rong, and Su She led Yan troops to rebel in Yan territory.

value.zh: 趙以靈丘封楚相春申君。
value.en: Zhao enfeoffed the Lord of Chunshen, the chancellor of Chu, with the city of Lingqiu.
value.literal: Zhao enfeoffed Lingqiu to Chu's chancellor Lord Chunshen.

value.zh: 真宗應符稽古神功讓德文明武定章聖元孝皇帝，諱恆，太宗第三子也。
value.en: Emperor Zhenzong—full posthumous style Responding to the Signs through Primordially Filial—whose personal name was Heng, was Taizong's third son.
value.literal: Emperor Zhenzong, entitled Responding to the Signs, Examining Antiquity, Divine Merit, Yielding Virtue, Civil and Bright, Martial and Settled, Manifest and Sagely, Primordially Filial, taboo name Heng, was the third son of Emperor Taizong.

value.zh: 母曰元德皇后李氏。
value.en: His mother was Lady Li, later honored as Empress Yuande.
value.literal: His mother was Empress Yuande, née Li.

value.zh: 初，乾德五年，五星從鎮星聚奎。
value.en: Legend dated his destiny to Qiande year five, when the five planets trailed Jupiter into a cluster at the Kui asterism.
value.literal: At the beginning, in the fifth year of Qiande, the five planets followed Saturn to gather at Kui.

value.zh: 明年正月，后夢以裾承日，有娠，十二月二日生于開封府第，赤光照室，左足指有文成「天」字。
value.en: The next spring his mother dreamed the sun rested in her lap; she conceived, and on the second of the twelfth month delivered him at the Kaifeng mansion in a room flooded with red light—on his left great toe the skin bore the character "Heaven."
value.literal: In the first month of the following year the empress dreamed that her skirt caught the sun; she became pregnant, and on the second day of the twelfth month gave birth at the Kaifeng commandery residence; red light filled the chamber, and on the left great toe a pattern formed the character "Heaven."

value.zh: 冬十月甲辰，雷有終大敗賊黨，復益州，殺三千餘人。
value.en: On jiachen in the tenth month of winter Lei Youzhong routed the rebels, retook Yizhou, and slaughtered three thousand men.
value.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on jiachen, Lei Youzhong greatly defeated the bandit party, recovered Yizhou, and killed more than three thousand men.

value.zh: 壬子，綿、漢都巡檢、澄州刺史張思鈞削籍流封州。
value.en: On renzi Zhang Sijun, inspector of Mian-Han and prefect of Cheng, was disranked and banished to Fengzhou.
value.literal: On renzi, Mian and Han circuit inspector and Cheng prefecture prefect Zhang Sijun was struck from the rolls and exiled to Feng prefecture.

value.zh: 乙卯，幸元份宮視疾。
value.en: On yimao he called on the ailing Prince Yuan Fen.
value.literal: On yimao, he visited Prince Yuan Fen's palace to inquire after his illness.

value.zh: 令諸州兼群牧。
value.en: He required every prefecture to take charge of local herd administration.
value.literal: Ordered each prefecture concurrently to oversee the herd offices.

value.zh: 己未，濱州防禦使王榮削籍流均州。
value.en: On jiwei Wang Rong, defense commissioner of Binzhou, was disranked and sent to Junzhou.
value.literal: On jiwei, Binzhou defense commissioner Wang Rong was struck from the rolls and exiled to Jun prefecture.

value.zh: 己丑，雷有終追斬王均于富順監，禽其黨六千餘人。
value.en: On jichou Lei Youzhong ran Wang Jun down at Fushun Prison, took his head, and rounded up six thousand rebels.
value.literal: On jichou, Lei Youzhong pursued and beheaded Wang Jun at Fushun Prison and captured more than six thousand of his followers.

value.zh: 詔原川峽路繫囚雜犯死罪以下。
value.en: He pardoned every Sichuan prisoner below capital grade implicated in the rebellion.
value.literal: An edict pardoned mixed offenders in Sichuan and the mountain passes below capital crime.

value.zh: 雷有終等以功進秩有差。
value.en: Lei Youzhong and his officers received graded promotions for the victory.
value.literal: Lei Youzhong and others were promoted in rank according to merit.

value.zh: 丙寅，以翰林學士王欽若、知制誥梁顥分為川、峽安撫使。
value.en: On bingyin he sent Wang Qinruo and Liang Hao to pacify Sichuan and the mountain passes as paired commissioners.
value.literal: On bingyin, Hanlin Academician Wang Qinruo and drafting drafter Liang Hao were made Sichuan and mountain-pass pacification commissioners respectively.

value.zh: 延州言破大盧、小盧等十族，獲人畜二十萬。
value.en: Yanzhou reported crushing the great and lesser Lu confederations and eight allied tribes, taking two hundred thousand captives and animals.
value.literal: Yanzhou reported defeating the great Lu and lesser Lu tribes and ten others, capturing two hundred thousand head of men and livestock.

value.zh: 劉福，徐州下邳人。
value.en: Liu Fu was from Xiapi in Xuzhou.
value.literal: Liu Fu was a native of Xiapi in Xuzhou.

value.zh: 少倜儻，魁岸有膂力。
value.en: As a young man he was bold and unconventional, tall and powerfully built.
value.literal: In youth he was unrestrained and free-spirited, with a towering frame and great physical strength.

value.zh: 周顯德中，世宗征淮南，福徒步謁見於壽春。
value.en: During the Xiande reign of the Later Zhou, when Emperor Shizong campaigned against Huainan, Fu walked to Shouchun to seek an audience.
value.literal: In the Xiande era of Zhou, when the Shizong Emperor campaigned against Huainan, Fu went on foot to present himself at Shouchun.

value.zh: 世宗奇之，因留麾下。
value.en: The emperor was struck by him and kept him in his retinue.
value.literal: The Shizong Emperor regarded him as extraordinary and therefore kept him in his personal following.

value.zh: 每出戰，則令福率衛士為先鋒，與破紫金山砦。
value.en: On every campaign he had Fu lead the imperial guards as vanguard; together they took the Zijin Mountain fort.
value.literal: Whenever he went out to battle, he would have Fu lead the bodyguard as vanguard, and together they captured the Zijin Mountain stockade.

value.zh: 淮南平，錄功授懷德指揮使。
value.en: After Huainan was pacified, his service was recognized with appointment as commander of the Huaide regiment.
value.literal: When Huainan was pacified, his merit was recorded and he was appointed commander of the Huaide command.

value.zh: 端拱初，遷龍衛都指揮使，領長州團練使，出鎮真定。
value.en: At the start of the Duan Gong era he was made commander of the Longwei guard and regimental commissioner of Changzhou, and posted to garrison Zhending.
value.literal: At the beginning of Duan Gong he was transferred to commander of Longwei, concurrently regimental commissioner of Changzhou, and went out to garrison Zhending.

value.zh: 是年秋，出為潁州防禦使。
value.en: That autumn he was posted as defense commissioner of Yingzhou.
value.literal: That autumn he went out as defense commissioner of Yingzhou.

value.zh: 未幾，太宗以其練習戎旅，特置龍衛、神衛四廂都指揮使以授之。
value.en: Soon afterward Taizong, recognizing his mastery of military affairs, specially created the four-division commands of Longwei and Shenwei and appointed him to lead them.
value.literal: Before long Taizong, because of his mastery of military affairs, specially created the four-division commanders of Longwei and Shenwei and invested him with the post.

value.zh: 改領振州防禦使。
value.en: He was concurrently made defense commissioner of Zhenzhou.
value.literal: He was changed to concurrently defense commissioner of Zhenzhou.

value.zh: 明年，拜殿前都虞候，領容州觀察使。
value.en: The following year he was made chief adjutant of the Palace Front Command and concurrently observation commissioner of Rongzhou.
value.literal: The next year he was appointed chief adjutant of the Palace Front Command and concurrently observation commissioner of Rongzhou.

value.zh: 一日，侍宴北苑，上入玄武門，守正大醉，與王榮論邊功於駕前，忿爭失儀，侍臣請以屬吏，上弗許。
value.en: One day at a feast in the Northern Park, as the emperor passed through the Xuanwu Gate, Shouzheng, very drunk, argued with Wang Rong over frontier exploits before the imperial carriage, quarreling loudly and forgetting decorum; attendants asked that they be turned over to the judicial authorities, but the emperor refused.
value.literal: One day, while attending a feast in the Northern Park, as the emperor entered the Xuanwu Gate, Shouzheng was greatly drunk and with Wang Rong disputed frontier merit before the imperial carriage, quarreling in anger and losing propriety; attendants asked that they be handed to the judicial officers, but the emperor would not permit it.

value.zh: 翌日，俱詣殿廷請罪，上曰：「朕亦大醉，漫不復省。」
value.en: The next day both came to court to apologize; the emperor said, "I was drunk myself and scarcely remember it."
value.literal: The next day they both came to the palace hall to plead guilty; the emperor said, "I too was greatly drunk and scarcely remember it."

value.zh: 遂釋不問。
value.en: He dismissed the matter without further inquiry.
value.literal: He then released them without inquiry.

value.zh: 俄命為定州行營副部署，受詔詣保州軍開道，遇敵於曹河，與戰數合，梟首三十餘，獲馬五十匹，上聞而壯之。
value.en: Soon afterward he was made deputy commander of the Dingzhou field headquarters and, by imperial order, sent to Ba prefecture to open a route. At Cao River he met the enemy and fought several engagements, taking more than thirty heads and fifty horses. When the emperor heard the report, he praised his martial spirit.
value.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed deputy commander of the Dingzhou field headquarters, received an edict to proceed to Ba prefecture army to open a route, encountered the enemy at Cao River, fought several engagements, took more than thirty heads, captured fifty horses; when the emperor heard of it he applauded his valor.

value.zh: 楊億，字大年，建州浦城人。
value.en: Yang Yi, styled Danian, came from Pucheng in Jianzhou.
value.literal: Yang Yi, courtesy name Danian, was a native of Pucheng in Jian Prefecture.

value.zh: 祖文逸，南唐玉山令。
value.en: His grandfather Yang Wenyi had served as magistrate of Yushan under the Southern Tang.
value.literal: His grandfather Wenyi was magistrate of Yushan under the Southern Tang.

value.zh: 億將生，文逸夢一道士，自稱懷玉山人來謁，未幾，億生，有毛被體，長尺餘，經月乃落。
value.en: Shortly before Yi's birth, Wenyi dreamed of a Daoist who introduced himself as the Hermit of Mount Huaiyu coming to call. Soon afterward Yi was born with hair covering his body, more than a foot in length, which did not fall away until a month had passed.
value.literal: Before Yi was to be born, Wenyi dreamed that a Daoist who called himself the Hermit of Huaiyu came to pay a visit; before long Yi was born, his body covered with hair more than a foot long, which fell off only after a month.

value.zh: 能言，母以小經口授，隨即成誦。
value.en: Once he could speak, his mother taught him the Minor Classics by recitation, and he mastered each passage as soon as he heard it.
value.literal: When he could speak, his mother orally taught him the Minor Classics, and he could recite them at once.

value.zh: 七歲，能屬文，對客談論，有老成風。
value.en: At seven he could already draft compositions, and when he conversed with guests he carried himself with uncanny maturity.
value.literal: At age seven he could compose prose; in conversation with guests he had the bearing of a seasoned man.

value.zh: 雍熙初，年十一，太宗聞其名，詔江南轉運使張去華就試詞藝，送闕下。
value.en: Early in the Yongxi era, when he was eleven, Emperor Taizong heard of him and ordered the Jiangnan transport commissioner Zhang Quhua to examine his literary gifts locally and escort him to court.
value.literal: Early in the Yongxi reign, at age eleven, Taizong heard his name and ordered the Jiangnan transport commissioner Zhang Quhua to test his literary skill on the spot and send him to the capital.

value.zh: 連三日得對，試詩賦五篇，下筆立成。
value.en: He was granted audience three days running and asked to produce five poems and fu compositions, each finished the moment he set brush to paper.
