value.literal: For three days in succession he was granted audience; he was tested with five poems and rhapsodies, each completed as soon as his brush touched the paper.

value.zh: 太宗深加賞異，命內侍都知王仁睿送至中書，又賦詩一章，宰相驚其俊異，削章為賀。
value.en: Taizong was deeply impressed and had the chief eunuch Wang Renrui escort him to the Secretariat. Yi also composed a poem of his own, and the chief ministers, astonished at his brilliance, reshaped their memorials into letters of congratulation.
value.literal: Taizong was deeply impressed and ordered the chief eunuch Wang Renrui to escort him to the Secretariat; he also composed a poem, and the chief ministers, astonished at his brilliance, trimmed their memorials into congratulations.

value.zh: 翌日，下制曰：「汝方髫齔，不由師訓，精爽神助，文字生知。
value.en: The next day an edict declared: "You are still a child, yet without formal schooling your mind is keen—as if heaven itself assisted you—and you know the written word as if born to it.
value.literal: The next day an edict was issued: "You are still in childhood, yet without instruction from teachers your spirit is keen and divinely aided, and you know writing by innate gift.

value.zh: 越景絕塵，一日千里，予有望於汝也。」
value.en: You leave the common herd far behind, advancing a thousand li in a single day. I place great hope in you."
value.literal: You outstrip the scene and leave the dust behind, a thousand li in a day; I have high hopes for you."

value.zh: 即授秘書省正字，特賜袍笏。
value.en: He was immediately appointed corrector in the Secretariat and was specially granted court robe and tablet.
value.literal: He was at once appointed corrector in the Secretariat and specially granted robe and tablet.

value.zh: 俄丁外艱，服除，會從祖徽之知許州，億往依焉。
value.en: Soon afterward he entered mourning for his father. When the mourning period ended, his father's cousin Yang Huizhi was serving as prefect of Xuzhou, and Yi went to stay with him.
value.literal: Before long he mourned his father's death; when the mourning ended, his father's cousin Huizhi was prefect of Xuzhou, and Yi went to live with him.

value.zh: 務學，晝夜不息，徽之間與語，歎曰：「興吾門者在汝矣。」
value.en: He applied himself to study without pause by day or night. When Huizhi spoke with him privately he sighed and said, "You are the one who will restore our family's fortunes."
value.literal: He devoted himself to study day and night without rest; when Huizhi spoke with him in private he sighed and said, "The one who will raise our house is you."

value.zh: 「臣嘗讀史，見漢武北築朔方之郡，平津侯諫，以為罷敝中國，以奉無用之地，願罷之。
value.en: "I have read in the histories that when Emperor Wu of Han established the northern commandery of Shuofang, the Marquis of Pingjin remonstrated, arguing that it would exhaust the empire to sustain a worthless region and urging that the project be abandoned.
value.literal: "Your servant has read history and seen that when Emperor Wu of Han built the northern commandery of Shuofang, the Marquis of Pingjin remonstrated, holding that it would exhaust China to supply a useless region and asking that it be abandoned.

value.zh: 上使辯士朱買臣等發十策以難平津，平津不能對。
value.en: The emperor had the debater Zhu Maichen and others raise ten counterarguments to confound the marquis, and he could not answer them.
value.literal: The emperor had the debater Zhu Maichen and others raise ten objections to confound Pingjin, and Pingjin could not reply.

value.zh: 臣以為平津為賢相，非不能折買臣之舌，蓋所以將順人君之意爾。
value.en: I believe Pingjin was a worthy minister. It was not that he could not refute Zhu Maichen's arguments, but that he chose to align himself with the emperor's wishes.
value.literal: Your servant holds that Pingjin was a worthy minister and was not unable to refute Maichen's tongue; he was simply accommodating the ruler's intent.

value.zh: 舊稱朔方，地在要荒之外，聲教不及。
value.en: Shuofang, as it was known in antiquity, lay beyond the outer marches, where the court's civilizing influence did not reach.
value.literal: Shuofang was so called of old; its land lay beyond the outer marches, where civilizing influence did not reach.

value.zh: 元朔中，大將軍衛青奮兵掠地，列置郡縣。
value.en: During the Yuanshuo reign period the Grand General Wei Qing campaigned vigorously, seized territory, and established a network of commanderies and counties.
value.literal: In the Yuanshuo era the Grand General Wei Qing took the field vigorously, seized territory, and set up commanderies and counties in array.

value.zh: 今靈州蓋朔方之故墟，僻介西鄙，數百里間無有水草，烽火亭障不相望。
value.en: Lingzhou today occupies roughly the old ground of Shuofang. It stands remote on the western frontier, and for hundreds of li there is neither water nor pasture; beacon towers and frontier posts cannot even see one another.
value.literal: Present-day Lingzhou is roughly the old site of Shuofang, remote on the western border; for several hundred li there is no water or grass, and beacon towers and frontier posts cannot see one another.

value.zh: 當其道路不壅，饢饋無虞，猶足以張大國之威聲，為中原之扞蔽。
value.en: When its roads were open and supply lines secure, it could still magnify the empire's prestige and serve as a bulwark for the heartland.
value.literal: When its roads were not blocked and supply trains were secure, it could still magnify the great state's prestige and serve as a shield for the central plain.

value.zh: 自邊境屢驚，凶黨猖熾，爵賞之而不恭，討罰之而無獲。
value.en: Since the frontier has been repeatedly alarmed, the hostile bands have grown ever bolder. Honors and rewards win no deference from them, and punitive campaigns yield no captives.
value.literal: Since the frontier has been repeatedly alarmed, the hostile bands have grown rampant; ennobled and rewarded, they show no deference; punished in campaigns, they are not taken.

value.zh: 自曹光實、白守榮、馬紹忠及王榮之敗，資糧屝屨，所失至多，將士丁夫，相枕而死。
value.en: Since the defeats suffered by Cao Guangshi, Bai Shourong, Ma Shaozhong, and Wang Rong, supplies and transport have been lost on a vast scale, and soldiers and corvée laborers have died in heaps upon the roads.
value.literal: Since the defeats of Cao Guangshi, Bai Shourong, Ma Shaozhong, and Wang Rong, supplies and transport have been lost in great measure, and soldiers and corvée laborers have died piled upon one another.

value.zh: 以至募商人輸帛入穀，償價數倍；
value.en: Matters have reached the point where merchants are recruited to deliver grain in exchange for silk, with reimbursement several times the market price;
value.literal: Matters have reached the point of recruiting merchants to bring silk in exchange for grain, with reimbursement several times the cost;

value.zh: 孤壤築城，邊民繹騷，國帑匱乏，不能制邊人之命，及濟靈武之急。
value.en: fortresses are raised on barren ground, frontier populations are in constant uproar, the national treasury is exhausted, and the court can neither command the border peoples nor relieve the crisis at Lingwu.
value.literal: fortresses are built on barren soil, frontier people are in constant turmoil, the national treasury is depleted, and the court cannot command the border peoples or relieve the crisis at Lingwu.

value.zh: 數年之間，凶黨逾盛。
value.en: Within a few years the hostile bands have grown stronger still.
value.literal: Within a few years the hostile bands have grown ever stronger.

value.zh: 靈武危堞，巋然僅存，河外五城，繼聞陷沒。
value.en: Lingwu's perilous walls stand alone, barely intact, while the five cities beyond the river have fallen one after another.
value.literal: Lingwu's perilous walls stand alone, barely surviving; the five cities beyond the river have fallen one after another.

value.zh: 但堅壁清野，坐食糗糧，閉壘枕戈，苟度朝夕，未粕出一兵，馳一騎，敢與之角。
value.en: The garrison merely fortifies its walls and clears the countryside, consumes stored grain, closes the forts and sleeps on its weapons, barely surviving from day to day, never venturing forth with a single soldier or rider to contest the enemy.
value.literal: They only fortify walls and clear the countryside, sit consuming dried grain, close the forts and sleep on their weapons, barely passing day and night, never sending forth a single soldier or rider to dare contest the enemy.

value.zh: 此靈武之存無益，明矣。
value.en: It is plain that holding Lingwu serves no purpose.
value.literal: That holding Lingwu is of no benefit is clear.

value.zh: 平津所言罷敝中國以奉無用之地，正今日謂也。
value.en: What the Marquis of Pingjin said about exhausting the empire to sustain a worthless region applies exactly to our situation today.
value.literal: What Pingjin said about exhausting China to supply a useless region is precisely what applies today.

value.zh: 孝靜皇帝，諱善見，清河文宣王亶之世子也，母曰胡妃。
value.en: Xiaojing Emperor bore the taboo name Shanjian. He was heir to Prince Wenxuan of Qinghe, Dan; his mother was Lady Hu.
value.literal: Xiaojing Emperor bore the taboo name Shanjian; he was the heir of Prince Wenxuan of Qinghe, Dan; his mother was Consort Hu.

value.zh: 永熙三年，拜通直散騎侍郎，八月，為驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。
value.en: In the third year of Yongxi he became direct-palace scattered cavalier attendant; in the eighth month he was made general of agile cavalry with an opening office equal in honor to the Three Excellencies.
value.literal: In the third year of Yongxi he was appointed direct-palace scattered cavalier attendant; in the eighth month he was made general of agile cavalry, opening-office equal-to-three-division commander.

value.zh: 出帝既入關，齊獻武王奉迎不克，乃與百僚會議，推帝以奉肅宗之後，時年十一。
value.en: After the western-departing emperor entered the passes, Gao Huan, Prince Xianwu of Qi tried to welcome him back and failed. He then convened the ministers and enthroned the boy to carry on the line of Emperor Suzong—eleven years old.
value.literal: When the emperor who had gone west had entered the passes, Gao Huan, Prince Xianwu of Qi went to welcome him but could not succeed; he then met with the hundred officials in council and set up the emperor to continue the line after Emperor Suzong—he was eleven years old.

value.zh: 從容雅服不得以矛釤從事 北史卷五「矛釤」作「務衫」。
value.en: Easy and elegant dress may not be used for spear and halberd affairs Northern History volume 5 reads "spear and halberd" as "service shirt."
value.literal: Easy and elegant dress may not be used to engage in spear and halberd affairs Northern History, volume 5, reads "spear and halberd" as "service shirt."

value.zh: 張森楷云：「一作『絳衫』。」
value.en: Zhang Senkai says: "Another reading is crimson shirt."
value.literal: Zhang Senkai says: "Another reading is crimson shirt."

value.zh: 按「釤」是刀名，作「矛釤」也可通。
value.en: Comment: "halberd" is a blade name; "spear and halberd" can also make sense.
value.literal: Comment: "halberd" is a blade name; "spear and halberd" can also make sense.

value.zh: 「務衫」不可考。
value.en: "Service shirt" cannot be verified.
value.literal: "Service shirt" cannot be verified.

value.zh: 絳衫是戎服，南齊書卷四七王融傳說他「戎服絳衫」，同書卷七一崔慧景附崔恭祖傳有「禿馬絳衫，手刺倒賊」之文。
value.en: Crimson shirt is military dress; Southern Qi Shu volume 47, Wang Rong's biography, says he "wore military dress, crimson shirt," and volume 71, Cui Huizong with Cui Gongzu attached, has "bare horse, crimson shirt, hand stabbed the fallen bandit."
value.literal: Crimson shirt is military dress; the Southern Qi Shu, volume 47, biography of Wang Rong, says he "wore military dress, crimson shirt," and the same book, volume 71, biography of Cui Huizong with attached biography of Cui Gongzu, has "bare horse, crimson shirt, hand stabbed the fallen bandit."

value.zh: 上云「從容雅服」，下自當說不得戎服，作「絳衫」似較長。
value.en: Above it says "easy and elegant dress"; below it should forbid military dress—"crimson shirt" seems preferable.
value.literal: Above it says "easy and elegant dress"; below it should speak of not being allowed military dress—"crimson shirt" seems preferable.

value.zh: 但不知張所云「一作」是哪一個本子，今仍之。
value.en: But it is unknown which edition Zhang's "another reading" refers to; the received text is retained.
value.literal: But it is unknown which edition Zhang's "another reading" refers to; the received text is retained.

value.zh: 王肅 宋弁
value.en: Wang Su; Song Bian
value.literal: Wang Su; Song Bian

value.zh: 誦，字國章，肅長兄融之子。
value.en: Song, whose courtesy name was Guozhang, was the son of Su's elder brother Rong.
value.literal: Song, styled Guozhang, was the son of Su's elder brother Rong.

value.zh: 學涉有文才，神氣清儁，風流甚美。
value.en: He was learned and gifted in letters, with a clear and handsome presence and an exceptionally refined bearing.
value.literal: He studied broadly and had literary talent; his spirit was clear and handsome, and his bearing exceedingly fine.

value.zh: 自員外郎、司徒主簿，轉司徒屬、司空諮議、通直常侍、汝南王友。
value.en: He rose from Gentleman of the Palace and Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education to Attendant of the Minister of Education, Adviser to the Minister of Works, Direct Regular Attendant, and Companion to the Prince of Runan.
value.literal: From Gentleman of the Palace, Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education, he was transferred to Attendant of the Minister of Education, Adviser to the Minister of Works, Direct Regular Attendant, and Companion to the Prince of Runan.

value.zh: 遷司徒諮議，加前軍、散騎常侍、光祿大夫。
value.en: He was promoted to Adviser to the Minister of Education, with additional titles of Vanguard General, Attendant at the Palace Cadet, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
value.literal: He was promoted to Adviser to the Minister of Education, with additional titles of Vanguard General, Attendant at the Palace Cadet, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

value.zh: 出為左將軍、幽州刺史。
value.en: He was sent out as General of the Left and Inspector of You Province.
value.literal: He was sent out as General of the Left and Inspector of You Province.

value.zh: 未幾，徵為長兼祕書監，徙給事黃門侍郎。
value.en: Before long he was recalled as Senior Acting Director of the Palace Library, then transferred to Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
value.literal: Before long he was summoned as Senior Acting Director of the Palace Library, then transferred to Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

value.zh: 肅宗崩，靈太后之立幼主也，於時大赦，誦宣讀詔書，音制抑揚，風神疎秀，百僚傾屬，莫不歎美。
value.en: When Emperor Suzong died and Empress Dowager Ling installed the young emperor, a general amnesty was proclaimed. Song read the edict aloud with cadences rising and falling, his bearing open and refined. The officials all turned to him in admiration.
value.literal: When Suzong died and Empress Dowager Ling established the young ruler, there was at the time a great amnesty; Song read the edict aloud, his tones rising and falling, his bearing open and refined; the hundred officials turned to him, and none failed to sigh in admiration.

value.zh: 孝莊初，於河陰遇害，年三十七。
value.en: Early in the Xiaozhuang reign he was killed at Heyin, at the age of thirty-seven.
value.literal: At the beginning of Xiaozhuang, he met with violence at Heyin, aged thirty-seven.

value.zh: [3]贈驃騎大將軍、尚書左僕射、司空公、徐州刺史，諡曰文宣。
value.en: [3] He was posthumously made General of Agile Cavalry, Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Minister of Works, and Inspector of Xuzhou, with the posthumous title Wenhuan.
value.literal: [3] Posthumously granted General of Agile Cavalry, Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Minister of Works, and Inspector of Xuzhou; posthumous title Wenhuan.

value.zh: 誦弟衍，字文舒。
value.en: Song's younger brother Yan, whose courtesy name was Wenshu.
value.literal: Song's younger brother Yan, styled Wenshu.

value.zh: 名行器藝亞於誦。
value.en: His reputation, conduct, and abilities were second only to Song's.
value.literal: His reputation, conduct, talent, and skill were second to Song's.

value.zh: 自著作佐郎，稍遷尚書郎、員外常侍、司空諮議、光祿大夫、廷尉、揚州大中正、度支尚書，仍轉七兵，徙太常卿。
value.en: Starting as Assistant Gentleman of the Academy, he rose through Gentleman of the Imperial Secretariat, Acting Regular Attendant, Adviser to the Minister of Works, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Minister of Justice, Chief Rectifier of Yang Province, and Director of Revenue, then transferred to the Seven Troops and became Minister of Ceremonies.
value.literal: From Assistant Gentleman of the Academy he was gradually promoted to Gentleman of the Imperial Secretariat, Acting Regular Attendant, Adviser to the Minister of Works, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Minister of Justice, Chief Rectifier of Yang Province, Director of Revenue, then transferred to the Seven Troops, and moved to Minister of Ceremonies.

value.zh: 出為散騎常侍、征東將軍、西兗州刺史。
value.en: He was sent out as Attendant at the Palace Cadet, General Who Conquers the East, and Inspector of Western Yanzhou.
value.literal: He was sent out as Attendant at the Palace Cadet, General Who Conquers the East, and Inspector of Western Yanzhou.

value.zh: 衍屆治未幾，屬尒朱仲遠稱兵內向，州既路衝，為其攻逼。
value.en: Yan had been in office only a short time when Erzhu Zhongyuan raised troops and marched inward. The province lay on the main route and came under his attack.
value.literal: Yan had been in office only a short time when Erzhu Zhongyuan raised troops and marched inward; the province being on the main route, he was attacked and pressed by him.

value.zh: 衍不能守，為仲遠所擒，以其名望不害也，令其騎牛從軍，久乃見釋。
value.en: Yan could not hold the province and was captured by Zhongyuan. Because of his reputation he was not harmed, but was made to ride an ox with the army. Only after a long time was he released.
value.literal: Yan could not hold it and was captured by Zhongyuan; because of his reputation he was not harmed, but was made to ride an ox with the army; only after a long time was he released.

value.zh: 還洛，除車騎將軍、左光祿大夫。
value.en: On returning to Luoyang he was made General of the Chariots and Cavalry and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
value.literal: Returning to Luoyang, he was appointed General of the Chariots and Cavalry and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

value.zh: 孝靜初，轉侍中，將軍如故。
value.en: Early in the Xiaojing reign he was made Palace Attendant while retaining his general's title.
value.literal: At the beginning of Xiaojing, he was transferred to Palace Attendant; his general's title as before.

value.zh: 天平三年卒，年五十二。
value.en: In the third year of the Tianping reign he died, at the age of fifty-two.
value.literal: In the third year of Tianping he died, aged fifty-two.

value.zh: 敕給東園祕器、賵物三百段，贈使持節、都督青徐兗三州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、尚書令、司徒公、徐州刺史，諡曰文獻。
value.en: An edict granted the secret funerary vessels of the Eastern Garden and three hundred sections of funeral goods. He was posthumously made Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in Qing, Xu, and Yan provinces, General of Agile Cavalry, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Minister of Education, and Inspector of Xuzhou, with the posthumous title Wenxian.
value.literal: An edict granted the secret funerary vessels of the Eastern Garden and three hundred sections of funeral goods; posthumously granted Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in the three provinces of Qing, Xu, and Yan, General of Agile Cavalry, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Minister of Education, and Inspector of Xuzhou; posthumous title Wenxian.

value.zh: 衍篤於交舊，有故人竺虩，於西兗為仲遠所害，其妻子飢寒，衍置之於家，累年贍恤，世人稱其敦厚。
value.en: Yan was devoted to old friends. An acquaintance named Zhu Xi had been killed by Zhongyuan in Western Yanzhou, leaving his wife and children hungry and cold. Yan took them into his household and supported them for years, and the world praised his generosity.
value.literal: Yan was devoted to old friends; he had an old acquaintance Zhu Xi who was killed by Zhongyuan in Western Yanzhou; his wife and children were hungry and cold; Yan took them into his household and for years provided support; the world praised his generosity.

value.zh: 遷中書侍郎，兼員外常侍，使於蕭賾。
value.en: He was promoted to Palace Attendant and Acting Regular Attendant and sent on a mission to Xiao Ze.
value.literal: He was promoted to Palace Attendant and concurrently Acting Regular Attendant, and sent on mission to Xiao Ze.

value.zh: 賾司徒蕭子良、祕書丞王融等皆稱美之，以為志氣謇烈不逮李彪，而體韻和雅、舉止閑邃過之。
value.en: Xiao Ze's Minister of Education Xiao Ziliang, Secretary Wang Rong, and others all praised him, finding that in resolve and boldness he did not match Li Biao, but in grace of manner and refined bearing he surpassed him.
value.literal: Ze's Minister of Education Xiao Ziliang, Secretary of the Palace Library Wang Rong, and others all praised him, considering that in resolve and spirit, forthrightness and fierceness, he did not match Li Biao, but in bodily grace and harmony, elegance of manner and leisurely depth, he surpassed him.

value.zh: 轉散騎侍郎，時散騎位在中書之右。
value.en: He was transferred to Attendant at the Palace Cadet, whose rank at the time stood above that of the Palace Secretariat.
value.literal: He was transferred to Attendant at the Palace Cadet; at the time the Palace Cadet's rank stood to the right of the Palace Secretariat.

value.zh: 高祖曾論江左事，因問弁曰：「卿比南行，入其隅隩，彼政道云何？
value.en: The Emperor Gaozu once discussed affairs south of the Yangtze and asked Bian: 'On your recent mission south you entered their inner circles—how is their governance?
value.literal: The Emperor Gaozu once discussed affairs south of the Yangtze and therefore asked Bian: 'On your recent journey south, you entered their inner recesses—how is their governance?

value.zh: 興亡之數可得知不？」
value.en: Can one discern the signs of their rise or fall?'
value.literal: Can the numbers of rise and fall be known?'

value.zh: 弁對曰：「蕭氏父子無大功於天下，既以逆取，不能順守。
value.en: Bian replied: 'The Xiao father and son have won no great merit for the realm. Having seized power by rebellion, they cannot preserve it through proper governance.
value.literal: Bian replied: 'The Xiao father and son have no great merit for the realm; having seized power by rebellion, they cannot preserve it by compliance.

value.zh: 德政不理，徭役滋劇，內無股肱之助，外有怨叛之民，以臣觀之，必不能貽厥孫謀，保有南海。
value.en: Their virtuous governance is in disorder and corvée labor grows ever heavier. Within they lack loyal ministers; without they face resentful and rebellious subjects. In my view they cannot bequeath lasting plans to their descendants or long hold the south.
value.literal: Virtuous governance is not ordered; corvée labor grows ever heavier; within they have no helpers as arms and thighs; without they have resentful and rebellious people—in my view they surely cannot bequeath plans to their descendants or long hold the southern sea.

value.zh: 若物憚其威，身免為幸。」
value.en: If men fear their might, merely to escape with one's life is already fortunate.'
value.literal: If creatures fear their might, to escape with one's person is already fortunate.'

value.zh: 蕭瑀瑀從子:鈞 鈞兄子:嗣業 瓘子:嵩 嵩子:華 嵩孫:復 華孫:俛 華孫:倣 倣子:廩 復曾孫:遘 瑀曾孫:定
value.en: Xiao Yu; his nephew's son Jun; Jun's elder brother's son Siye; Guan's son Song; Song's son Hua; Song's grandson Fu; Hua's grandsons Mian and Fang; Fang's son Lin; Fu's great-grandson Gou; and Yu's great-grandson Ding.
value.literal: Xiao Yu; Yu's nephew's son: Jun; Jun's elder brother's son: Siye; Guan's son: Song; Song's son: Hua; Song's grandson: Fu; Hua's grandson: Mian; Hua's grandson: Fang; Fang's son: Lin; Fu's great-grandson: Gou; Yu's great-grandson: Ding.

value.zh: 子廩，字富侯。
value.en: His son Lin, styled Fuhou.
value.literal: His son Lin, style name Fuhou.

value.zh: 第進士，遷尚書郎。
value.en: He passed the jinshi and was appointed a Secretariat official.
value.literal: He placed in the jinshi examination and was transferred to a Secretariat official.

value.zh: 仿領南海，解官往侍。
value.en: When Fang took the post in the far south, Lin resigned his own office to accompany and care for him.
value.literal: When Fang took charge of the Southern Sea, he resigned office to go and attend him.

value.zh: 為人退約少合。
value.en: By nature he was modest and reserved, and made few close friends.
value.literal: As a man he was retiring and restrained, seldom in accord with others.

value.zh: 南海多穀紙，仿敕諸子繕補殘書。
value.en: Paper was plentiful in the south, and Fang had his sons repair damaged books from his library.
value.literal: The Southern Sea had much grain-straw paper; Fang ordered his sons to mend and repair damaged books.

value.zh: 廩諫曰：「州距京師且萬里，書成不可露齎，必貯以囊笥，貪者伺望，得無薏苡嫌乎？」
value.en: Lin objected: "This post is ten thousand li from the capital. Finished books cannot be carried openly—they must be packed in chests, and the greedy will take notice. Will you not invite the suspicion Ma Yuan suffered over his Job's-tears?"
value.literal: Lin remonstrated: "The prefecture is nearly ten thousand li from the capital; when books are finished they cannot be carried openly—they must be stored in bags and cases, and the greedy will watch and wait. Will there not be the suspicion of the Job's-tears incident?"

value.zh: 仿曰：「善，吾思不及此。」
value.en: Fang said, "You are right; I had not thought of that."
value.literal: Fang said: "Good—I did not think as far as this."

value.zh: 乃止。
value.en: He dropped the plan.
value.literal: Thereupon he stopped.

value.zh: 廣明初，以諫議大夫知制誥，請厲止夜行以備賊諜，出太倉粟賤估以濟貧民。
value.en: Early in the Guangming era, as Remonstrating Grandee and edict drafter, he urged a strict curfew against rebel spies and the sale of imperial grain at low prices to aid the poor.
value.literal: At the beginning of Guangming, as Remonstrating Grandee he drafted edicts; he requested stern prohibition of night travel to guard against rebel spies, and release of Great Granary grain at low valuation to relieve the poor.

value.zh: 俄遷京兆尹。
value.en: He was soon made metropolitan governor of the capital district.
value.literal: Soon he was transferred to Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao.

value.zh: 田令孜養子有罪亡，擊捕吏，系獄，請救踵門，廩不納，杖殺之，內外畏讋。
value.en: An adopted son of Tian Lingzi committed a crime and fled; he assaulted the arresting officer and was jailed. Supplicants thronged Lin's gate, but he refused them and had the man flogged to death; court and capital alike stood in awe.
value.literal: Tian Lingzi's adopted son committed a crime and fled; he struck the arresting officer and was imprisoned. Pleas for rescue came in succession at the gate; Lin would not accept them and had him beaten to death. Within and without, all feared and submitted.

value.zh: 令孜拒黃巢，以廩為糧料使，辭疾，貶賀州司戶參軍事。
value.en: When Lingzi resisted Huang Chao he named Lin grain commissioner; Lin pleaded illness and was demoted to registrar at Hezhou.
value.literal: Lingzi resisted Huang Chao and appointed Lin grain commissioner; Lin pleaded illness and was demoted to Registrar of He Prefecture.

value.zh: 會襄王竊據，挈族逃河朔，鎮冀節度使王鎔厚禮之。
value.en: When the Prince of Xiang seized power, Lin fled north with his family; Wang Rong, governor of Zhenji, received him with great honor.
value.literal: When the Prince of Xiang seized territory by force, he took his clan and fled to the Hebei region; Wang Rong, military governor of Zhenji, treated him with generous courtesy.

value.zh: 光化中，以給事中召，不至，卒。
value.en: In the Guanghua era he was recalled as Supervising Censor but did not come; he died.
value.literal: During Guanghua he was summoned as Supervising Censor but did not arrive; he died.

value.zh: 二王諸葛李孟
value.en: The Two Wangs, Zhu, Ge, Li, and Meng
value.literal: The Two Wangs, Zhu, Ge, Li, and Meng

value.zh: 方立倚朱全忠為助，故克用擊邢、洺、磁無虛歲，地為鬥場，人不能稼。
value.en: Fangli relied on Zhu Quanzhong for support, so Keyong attacked Xing, Ming, and Ci almost every year; the land became a battlefield and farming ceased.
value.literal: Fangli relied on Zhu Quanzhong for aid, so Keyong attacked Xing, Ming, and Ci year after year without pause; the land became a battleground and people could not farm.

value.zh: 光啟二年，克修擊邢州取故鎮，進攻武安。
value.en: In the second year of Guangqi, Kexiu attacked Xing Prefecture, recovered the old seat, and advanced on Wu'an.
value.literal: In the second year of Guangqi, Kexiu attacked Xing Prefecture, recovered the old seat, and advanced against Wu'an.

value.zh: 方立將呂臻、馬爽戰焦岡，為克修所破，斬首萬級，執臻等，拔武安、臨洺、邯鄲、沙河。
value.en: Fangli's generals Lü Zhen and Ma Shuang fought at Jiaogang and were routed by Kexiu; ten thousand heads were taken, Zhen and others captured, and Wu'an, Linming, Handan, and Shahe fell.
value.literal: Fangli's generals Lü Zhen and Ma Shuang fought at Jiaogang and were defeated by Kexiu; ten thousand heads were cut off, Zhen and others were captured, and Wu'an, Linming, Handan, and Shahe were taken.

value.zh: 克用以安金俊為邢州刺史，招撫之。
value.en: Keyong appointed An Jinjun governor of Xing Prefecture to pacify the region.
value.literal: Keyong appointed An Jinjun governor of Xing Prefecture to win the people over.

value.zh: 方立丐兵於王镕，镕以兵三萬赴之，克修還。
value.en: Fangli begged Wang Rong for troops; Rong sent thirty thousand men, and Kexiu withdrew.
value.literal: Fangli begged troops from Wang Rong; Rong sent thirty thousand men to his aid, and Kexiu withdrew.

value.zh: 後二年，方立督部將奚忠信兵三萬攻遼州，以金啖赫連鐸與連和。
value.en: Two years later Fangli led his subordinate Xi Zhongxin with thirty thousand men against Liao Prefecture and bribed Helian Duo with gold to join him.
value.literal: Two years later Fangli supervised his subordinate Xi Zhongxin with thirty thousand troops to attack Liao Prefecture, bribing Helian Duo with gold to join in alliance.

value.zh: 會契丹攻鐸，師失期，忠信三分其兵，鼓而行，克用伏兵於險，忠信前軍沒。
value.en: The Khitans attacked Duo and the army missed its rendezvous. Zhongxin divided his force in three and advanced with drums beating. Keyong ambushed them in a defile and destroyed the vanguard.
value.literal: It happened that the Khitans attacked Duo; the army missed its rendezvous. Zhongxin divided his force in three and advanced with drums beating. Keyong ambushed in a defile and Zhongxin's vanguard was wiped out.

value.zh: 既戰，大敗，執忠信，餘眾走，脫歸者才十二。
value.en: They were routed in battle; Zhongxin was captured, the rest fled, and only twelve men made it back alive.
value.literal: After the battle they were greatly defeated; Zhongxin was captured, the rest fled, and only twelve men escaped back alive.

value.zh: 龍紀元年，克用使李罕之、李存孝擊邢，攻磁、洺，方立戰琉璃陂，大敗，禽其二將，被斧锧，徇邢壘，呼曰：「孟公速降，有能斬其首者，假三州節度使！」
value.en: In the first year of Longji, Keyong sent Li Hanzhi and Li Cunxiao against Xing and Ci-Ming. Fangli fought at Liuli Po and was routed; two generals were captured, shackled, and paraded before the Xing ramparts with the cry, "Lord Meng, surrender at once! Whoever cuts off his head shall govern the three prefectures!"
value.literal: In the first year of Longji, Keyong sent Li Hanzhi and Li Cunxiao to attack Xing and assault Ci and Ming. Fangli fought at Liuli Po and was greatly defeated; his two generals were captured, put in cangue and stocks, and paraded before the Xing ramparts with the cry, "Lord Meng, surrender quickly! Whoever can cut off his head shall be made provisional military governor of the three prefectures!"

value.zh: 方立力屈，又屬州殘墮，人心恐。
value.en: Fangli's strength was spent, the prefectures lay in ruins, and panic spread through the ranks.
value.literal: Fangli's strength was spent, and moreover the prefectures were ruined and collapsing; hearts were filled with fear.

value.zh: 性剛急，持下少恩，夜自行陴，兵皆倨，告勞。
value.en: Harsh and impatient by nature, he showed little kindness below. He patrolled the ramparts by night himself; the troops grew insolent and complained of exhaustion.
value.literal: By nature he was harsh and impatient, showing little kindness to subordinates. He walked the ramparts by night himself; the troops were all insolent and complained of exhaustion.

value.zh: 自顧不可復振，乃還，引冘殺。
value.en: Seeing he could not recover, he returned and hanged himself.
value.literal: Seeing that he could not rise again, he returned and took his own life by strangulation.

value.zh: ◎宦者下李輔國，本名靜忠，以閹奴為閑廄小兒。
value.en: Eunuchs, Part 2 — Li Fuguo. Li Fuguo, born Jingzhong, entered service as a young groom in the imperial spare stables in the capacity of a castrated bondsman.
value.literal: Eunuchs, Part 2 — Li Fuguo. Li Fuguo's original name was Jingzhong; as a castrated bondsman he served as a petty attendant in the spare stables.

value.zh: 貌佇陋，略通書計。
value.en: Homely and awkward in bearing, he knew a little of letters and accounts.
value.literal: His appearance was clumsy and ugly; he had a slight knowledge of writing and reckoning.

value.zh: 事高力士，年四十餘，使主廄中簿最。
value.en: Under Gao Lishi's patronage, he was assigned at forty-odd to keep the stable ledgers.
value.literal: He served Gao Lishi; when he was over forty, he was made to supervise the stable registers.

value.zh: 王鉷為使，以典禾豆，能檢擿耗欺，馬以故肥，薦之皇太子，得侍東宮。
value.en: Under Commissioner Wang Hong he oversaw grain and fodder, exposing shrinkage and fraud so diligently that the horses grew notably fat; recommended to the crown prince, he gained a post in the Eastern Palace.
value.literal: When Wang Hong was commissioner, he put him in charge of grain and fodder; able to detect waste and fraud, the horses thereby grew fat; he was recommended to the Crown Prince and obtained service in the Eastern Palace.

value.zh: 李克用引軍去，帝還京師。
value.en: Li Keyong withdrew his army, and the emperor returned to the capital.
value.literal: Li Keyong withdrew his army; the emperor returned to the capital.

value.zh: 胤、全忠議，盡誅第五可範等八百餘人於內侍省，哀號之聲聞於路，留單弱數十人，備宮中灑掃。
value.en: Yin and Quanzhong agreed to execute more than eight hundred men, including Diwu Kefan, entirely within the Palace Domestic Service. Their cries of grief were heard in the streets. A few dozen feeble ones were left for palace sweeping and cleaning.
value.literal: Yin and Quanzhong agreed to execute more than eight hundred men, including Diwu Kefan, entirely within the Palace Domestic Service. Their cries of grief were heard in the streets. A few dozen feeble ones were left for palace sweeping and cleaning.

value.zh: 胤以鎮人性謹厚，即詔王镕擇五十人為敕使，內諸司宦官主領者皆罷。
value.en: Yin held that men from the provinces were cautious and steady. An edict at once ordered Wang Rong to select fifty men as Imperial Dispatch Envoys, and all eunuch supervisors of the inner offices were dismissed.
value.literal: Yin held that men from the provinces were cautious and steady. An edict at once ordered Wang Rong to select fifty men as Imperial Dispatch Envoys. All eunuch supervisors of the inner offices were dismissed.

value.zh: 於是追諸道監軍，所在賜死，其財產籍入之。
value.en: Thereupon envoys were sent to recall the Military Supervisors from each circuit. Wherever found, they were granted death, and their property was registered and confiscated.
value.literal: Thereupon envoys were sent to recall the Military Supervisors from each circuit; wherever found, they were granted death. Their property was registered and confiscated.

value.zh: 詔以中官脅遷狀及全忠迎乘輿本末告方鎮，罷監軍院，咸視國初故事，以三十人為員，衣黃衣，不得養子。
value.en: An edict reported to the regional prefectures the circumstances of the eunuchs' coerced removal and the full account of Quanzhong's reception of the imperial carriage. The Supervisory Corps was abolished. All were to follow the founding precedents of the dynasty: a quota of thirty, wearing yellow robes, and forbidden to adopt sons.
value.literal: An edict reported to the regional prefectures the circumstances of the eunuchs' coerced removal and the full account of Quanzhong's reception of the imperial carriage. The Supervisory Corps was abolished. All were to follow the founding precedents of the dynasty: thirty as the quota, wearing yellow robes, forbidden to adopt sons.

value.zh: 內諸司皆歸省若寺，兩軍內外八鎮兵悉屬六軍。
value.en: The inner offices all reverted to ministries or directorates. Troops of the Two Armies, inner and outer, and the Eight Garrisons all came under the Six Armies.
value.literal: The inner offices all reverted to ministries or directorates. Troops of the Two Armies, inner and outer, and the Eight Garrisons all came under the Six Armies.

value.zh: 全忠還汴州，帝以第五可範等無辜，頗悼之，為文以祭。
value.en: Quanzhong returned to Bianzhou. The emperor, considering Diwu Kefan and the others innocent, mourned them deeply and composed a text to offer sacrifice.
value.literal: Quanzhong returned to Bianzhou. The emperor, considering Diwu Kefan and the others innocent, mourned them deeply and composed a text to offer sacrifice.

value.zh: 自是宣傳詔命，皆以宮人。
value.en: From this time forward, proclamations and edicts were all conveyed by palace women.
value.literal: From this time forward, proclamations and edicts were all conveyed by palace women.

value.zh: 沙陀，西突厥別部處月種也。
value.en: The Shatuo were a branch of the Chuyue people, a dependent tribe of the Western Turks.
value.literal: The Shatuo were of the Chuyue branch among the dependent tribes of the Western Turks.

value.zh: 始，突厥東西部分治烏孫故地，與處月、處蜜雜居。
value.en: In the beginning, as the Eastern and Western Turks partitioned the old Wusun territories, they dwelt alongside the Chuyue and Chumi peoples.
value.literal: At first, when the Eastern and Western Turks divided rule over the former Wusun lands, they lived intermixed with the Chuyue and Chumi.

value.zh: 貞觀七年，太宗以鼓纛立利邲咄陸可汗，而族人步真觖望，謀並其弟彌射乃自立。
value.en: In Zhenguan 7 (633), Emperor Taizong invested Ashina Yipiduolu as khan in the formal drum-and-banner ceremony. A clansman named Böke, resentful of the appointment, conspired to ally with his younger brother Mishe and seize power for himself.
value.literal: In the seventh year of Zhenguan, Taizong installed Ashina Yipiduolu as khan with the drum-and-banner ceremony; the clansman Böke was discontented and plotted to join his younger brother Mishe and declare himself ruler.

value.zh: 彌射懼，率處月等入朝。
value.en: Fearing for his safety, Mishe led the Chuyue and other tribes to present themselves at court.
value.literal: Mishe was afraid and led the Chuyue and others to submit to the court.

value.zh: 而步真勢窮，亦歸國。
value.en: Böke, his position hopeless, likewise submitted to the Tang.
value.literal: Böke, his strength exhausted, also returned to allegiance.

value.zh: 其留者，咄陸以射匱特勒劫越之子賀魯統之。
value.en: Those who stayed behind were placed under Helu, son of the Shegui tegin Jeučü, by Ashina Duolu.
value.literal: Those who remained were placed under Helu, son of the Shegui tegin Jeučü, by Ashina Duolu.

value.zh: 大順初，克用自攻赫連鐸於雲州，拔東郛。
value.en: Early in the Dashun era Keyong personally attacked Helian Duo at Yunzhou and captured the eastern suburb.
value.literal: At the beginning of Dashun, Keyong himself attacked Helian Duo at Yunzhou and took the eastern suburb.

value.zh: 幽州李匡威以兵三萬救之，殺其將安金俊，克用走。
value.en: Li Kuangwei of Youzhou brought thirty thousand men to the rescue, killed Keyong's general An Jinjun, and Keyong fled.
value.literal: Li Kuangwei of Youzhou brought thirty thousand to rescue him, killed his general An Jinjun, and Keyong fled.

value.zh: 鐸與匡威共建言：「山南亂，克用實首之。
value.en: Duo and Kuangwei jointly memorialized: "The turmoil in the southern mountains was chiefly Keyong's doing.
value.literal: Duo and Kuangwei jointly memorialized: "The turmoil in the southern mountains—Keyong was truly its author.

value.zh: 今乘其敗，可伐而取也。」
value.en: Now that he is defeated, he can be attacked and destroyed."
value.literal: Now, taking advantage of his defeat, he can be attacked and taken."

value.zh: 全忠亦請與河北三鎮共討之。
value.en: Quanzhong likewise asked to join the three Hebei circuits in attacking him.
value.literal: Quanzhong also asked to join the three Hebei circuits in attacking him.

value.zh: 宰相張浚是其計，乃下制削克用官爵、屬籍，以浚為兵馬招討、制置、宣慰使，京兆尹孫揆副之，樞密使駱全諲為行營都監，華州節度使韓建為行營馬步都虞候兼供軍糧料使，王镕領河東東面，全忠南面，李匡威北面，並為行營招討使。
value.en: Chancellor Zhang Jun approved the plan. An edict stripped Keyong of office, rank, and clan register. Zhang Jun was appointed campaign commander, disposition commissioner, and pacification commissioner, with Jingzhao Prefect Sun Kui as deputy, Privy Councilor Luo Quanqian as campaign supervisor, and Huazhou Military Governor Han Jian as chief adjutant and provisions commissioner. Wang Rong commanded the eastern Hedong front, Quanzhong the south, and Li Kuangwei the north—all as campaign commanders.
value.literal: Chancellor Zhang Jun approved the plan; an edict stripped Keyong of office, rank, and clan register; Jun was made campaign commander for horse troops, disposition commissioner, and pacification commissioner; Jingzhao Prefect Sun Kui was his deputy; Privy Councilor Luo Quanqian was campaign supervisor; Huazhou Military Governor Han Jian was campaign horse-and-foot chief adjutant and army provisions commissioner; Wang Rong commanded the eastern Hedong front, Quanzhong the south, Li Kuangwei the north—all as campaign commanders.

value.zh: 鐸副匡威，先薄戰。
value.en: Duo served under Kuangwei and pressed the attack first.
value.literal: Duo served under Kuangwei and pressed the attack first.

value.zh: 克用追潞兵，不肯行，共殺守將李克恭，送款於汴，南首闕下。
value.en: Keyong pursued the Lu troops, but they refused to march, killed garrison commander Li Kejing, submitted to Bian, and turned south toward the palace.
value.literal: Keyong pursued the Lu troops; they refused to march; together they killed the garrison commander Li Kejing, sent submission to Bian, and turned south toward the palace.

value.zh: 更詔揆為昭義節度使，克用將李存孝邀揆長子殺之。
value.en: Sun Kui was reappointed military governor of Zhaoyi. Keyong's officer Li Cunxiao ambushed and killed Kui's eldest son.
value.literal: Sun Kui was reappointed military governor of Zhaoyi; Keyong's officer Li Cunxiao ambushed and killed Kui's eldest son.

value.zh: 匡威、鐸並吐蕃、黠戛斯眾十萬攻遮虜軍，殺其將劉胡子。
value.en: Kuangwei and Duo, with one hundred thousand Tibetan and Qarluk allies, attacked Zhelu Army and killed its commander Liu Huzi.
value.literal: Kuangwei and Duo with Tibetan and Qarluk forces numbering one hundred thousand attacked Zhelu Army and killed its commander Liu Huzi.

value.zh: 克用乃屯渾河川，存孝與鐸戰樂安，鐸敗走。
value.en: Keyong encamped on the Hun River. Cunxiao fought Duo at Le'an and drove him off.
value.literal: Keyong then encamped on the Hun River; Cunxiao fought Duo at Le'an; Duo was defeated and fled.

value.zh: 浚入陰地關，壁汾、隰，薛鐵山、李承嗣營洪洞迎戰。
value.en: Zhang Jun entered Yindi Pass and encamped at Fen and Xi. Xue Tieshan and Li Chengsi encamped at Hongdong to meet him.
value.literal: Jun entered Yindi Pass, walled at Fen and Xi; Xue Tieshan and Li Chengsi encamped at Hongdong to meet the attack.

value.zh: 存孝次趙城，韓建夜出壯士三百乘其營，存孝伏以待，建兵大奔。
value.en: Cunxiao halted at Zhaocheng. Han Jian sent three hundred stalwarts by night to strike his camp, but Cunxiao lay in wait and Jian's men fled in disorder.
value.literal: Cunxiao halted at Zhaocheng; Han Jian sent out three hundred stalwarts by night to strike his camp; Cunxiao lay in ambush; Jian's troops fled in great disorder.

value.zh: 存孝攻絳州，未下，晉州刺史張行恭棄城走，建與浚遁還。
value.en: Cunxiao attacked Jiangzhou without success. Jinzhou Prefect Zhang Xinggong abandoned his city and fled. Han Jian and Zhang Jun withdrew in defeat.
value.literal: Cunxiao attacked Jiangzhou but did not take it; Jinzhou Prefect Zhang Xinggong abandoned the city and fled; Jian and Jun slipped back.

value.zh: 明年，克用奉表自陳，乃復拜檢校太師、守中書令、隴西郡王。
value.en: The following year Keyong memorialized in his own defense and was restored as Acting Grand Preceptor, Keeper of the Secretariat, and Duke of Longxi.
value.literal: The next year Keyong memorialized in his own defense and was again appointed Acting Grand Preceptor, Keeper of the Secretariat, and Duke of Longxi.

value.zh: 景福初，鎮州王镕攻堯山，克用使李嗣勛擊之，斬級三萬，克用遂拔天長，略常山，度滹沱，燔其郛。
value.en: Early in the Jingfu era Wang Rong of Zhenzhou attacked Yaoshan. Keyong sent Li Sikuen against him and claimed thirty thousand heads. Keyong then took Tianchang, overran Changshan, crossed the Hutuo, and burned its outer walls.
value.literal: At the beginning of Jingfu, Wang Rong of Zhenzhou attacked Yaoshan; Keyong sent Li Sikuen against him and took thirty thousand heads; Keyong then took Tianchang, overran Changshan, crossed the Hutuo, and burned its outer walls.

value.zh: 徇地至趙，取鼓、槁二城。
value.en: He overran the country as far as Zhao and took the cities of Gu and Gao.
value.literal: He overran the land to Zhao and took the two cities of Gu and Gao.

value.zh: 赫連鐸眾八萬攻天成軍，克用飛檄發軍太原，匡威已壁雲州北郊，克用自神堆引軍夜入雲州，死戰，走之。
value.en: Helian Duo attacked Tiancheng Army with eighty thousand men. Keyong issued urgent orders from Taiyuan while Kuangwei had already encamped at the north suburb of Yunzhou. Keyong led his men by night from Shendui into Yunzhou, fought savagely, and drove him off.
value.literal: Helian Duo with eighty thousand attacked Tiancheng Army; Keyong sent urgent orders from Taiyuan; Kuangwei had already walled at the north suburb of Yunzhou; Keyong from Shendui led troops by night into Yunzhou, fought to the death, and drove him off.

value.zh: 乾寧元年，克用次新城，鐸膝行詣軍門降，克用鞭而縱之。
value.en: In Qianning 1 (894) Keyong halted at Xincheng. Duo came on his knees to the camp gate to surrender. Keyong whipped him and let him go.
value.literal: In the first year of Qianning, Keyong halted at Xincheng; Duo came on his knees to the camp gate to surrender; Keyong whipped him and let him go.

value.zh: 進下武州，攻新州。
value.en: He advanced to take Wuzhou and attacked Xinzhou.
value.literal: He advanced to take Wuzhou and attacked Xinzhou.

value.zh: 李匡籌引步騎七萬救之，克用迎戰，斬首萬級，俘少將三百，徇城下，新州降。
value.en: Li Kuangchou led seventy thousand foot and horse to the rescue. Keyong met him in battle, claimed ten thousand heads, took three hundred junior officers prisoner, overran the walls, and Xinzhou surrendered.
value.literal: Li Kuangchou led seventy thousand foot and horse to rescue it; Keyong met him in battle, took ten thousand heads, captured three hundred junior officers, overran below the walls, and Xinzhou surrendered.

value.zh: 取媯州，匡籌棄幽州走。
value.en: He took Guizhou. Kuangchou abandoned Youzhou and fled.
value.literal: He took Guizhou; Kuangchou abandoned Youzhou and fled.

value.zh: 明年，幽州降，克用以劉仁恭為留後，乃旋。
value.en: The following year Youzhou surrendered. Keyong appointed Liu Rengong acting commander and returned home.
value.literal: The next year Youzhou surrendered; Keyong made Liu Rengong acting commander and returned.

value.zh: 光化初，帝還京師，詔克用與全忠解仇，宰相徐彥若、崔胤皆勸之。
value.en: Early in the Guanghua era the emperor returned to the capital and ordered Keyong and Quanzhong to reconcile. Chancellors Xu Yanruo and Cui Yin both urged them to comply.
value.literal: Early in Guanghua, the emperor returned to the capital and ordered Keyong and Quanzhong to end their feud; chancellors Xu Yanruo and Cui Yin both urged it.

value.zh: 克用勢已折，然尚以功高位全忠上，恥先下之，時王镕方睦於汴，乃遺書镕，使為己倡。
value.en: Keyong's strength was already broken, yet he still outranked Quanzhong by merit and was ashamed to yield first. Wang Rong was then on friendly terms with Bian, so Keyong sent him a letter asking him to take the lead on his behalf.
value.literal: Keyong's power was already broken, yet he still outranked Quanzhong by merit and seniority and was ashamed to yield first; Wang Rong was then on friendly terms with Bian, so he sent Rong a letter asking him to take the lead for him.

value.zh: 全忠即遣使奉書幣恭甚，克用亦報之。
value.en: Quanzhong at once sent envoys bearing letters and gifts with great deference, and Keyong replied in kind.
value.literal: Quanzhong at once sent envoys bearing letters and gifts with great deference, and Keyong replied in kind.

value.zh: 然汴日益張，窮鬥不置。
value.en: Yet Bian grew stronger by the day, and their bitter struggle did not let up.
value.literal: Yet Bian grew stronger day by day, and their bitter struggle did not cease.

value.zh: 王珙請汴兵攻河中，克用使李嗣昭、張漢瑜援之，汴兵走。
value.en: Wang Gong asked Bian for troops to attack Hezhong. Keyong sent Li Cizhao and Zhang Hanyu to the rescue, and the Bian troops fled.
value.literal: Wang Gong asked Bian for troops to attack Hezhong; Keyong sent Li Cizhao and Zhang Hanyu to aid the defense, and the Bian troops fled.

value.zh: 葛從周取承天軍，氏叔琮取遼州、樂平，進壁榆次，克用使周德威逐出之。
value.en: Ge Congzhou took Chengtian Army. Shi Shuzong seized Liaozhou and Leping and advanced to encamp at Yuci. Keyong sent Zhou Dewei to drive them out.
value.literal: Ge Congzhou took Chengtian Army; Shi Shuzong took Liaozhou and Leping and advanced to encamp at Yuci; Keyong sent Zhou Dewei to drive them out.

value.zh: 李嗣昭以步騎三萬下太行，略河內，拔懷州，進攻河陽，汴人閻寶救之，嗣昭退保懷。
value.en: Li Cizhao descended the Taihang with thirty thousand infantry and cavalry, overran Henan Interior, took Huaizhou, and advanced on Heyang. Yan Bao of Bian came to the rescue, and Cizhao withdrew to hold Huai.
value.literal: Li Cizhao descended the Taihang with thirty thousand infantry and cavalry, overran Henan Interior, took Huaizhou, and advanced on Heyang; Yan Bao of Bian came to the rescue, and Cizhao withdrew to hold Huai.

value.zh: 天復元年，全忠取晉、絳，逼河中，王珂告急，使相望，汴人扼空道，晉兵不得前，遂虜珂。
value.en: In Tianfu 1 Quanzhong took Jin and Jiang and pressed Hezhong. Wang Ke sent urgent appeals, envoys arriving one after another, but Bian troops blocked the open road and Jin forces could not advance. Ke was captured.
value.literal: In the first year of Tianfu, Quanzhong took Jin and Jiang and pressed Hezhong; Wang Ke sent urgent appeals, envoys stretching in sight of one another; Bian troops blocked the open road and Jin troops could not advance, and Ke was captured.

value.zh: 珂妻，克用女，不能救，全忠遂有河中，克用朝貢道亦梗。
value.en: Ke's wife was Keyong's daughter, yet Keyong could not save him. Quanzhong thus gained Hezhong, and Keyong's tributary route was also cut off.
value.literal: Ke's wife was Keyong's daughter, yet he could not save her husband; Quanzhong thus gained Hezhong, and Keyong's tributary route was also blocked.

value.zh: 新五代史卷一 梁本紀第一
value.en: New History of the Five Dynasties, Volume 1: Basic Annals of Liang, Part One.
value.literal: New History of the Five Dynasties, Volume 1 — Basic Annals of Liang, Part One.

value.zh: 光化元年三月，天子以王兼天平軍節度使。
value.en: In the third month of Guanghua 1 (898) the court added the Tianping command to Quanzhong's titles.
value.literal: In the third month of the first year of Guanghua the Son of Heaven made Quanzhong concurrently military governor of the Tianping army.

value.zh: 四月，遣葛從周攻晉之山東，取邢、洺、磁三州。
value.en: In the fourth month he sent Ge Congzhou into Hedong's Shandong districts and seized Xing, Ming, and Ci.
value.literal: In the fourth month he sent Ge Congzhou to attack Hedong's Shandong region and took Xing, Ming, and Ci prefectures.

value.zh: 襄州趙匡凝自其父德諲時來附，匡凝又與楊行密、李克用通，而其事泄。
value.en: Zhao Kuangning of Xiangzhou had been a vassal since his father Deyin's day. He was now in touch with Yang Xingmi and Li Keyong, and the traffic was discovered.
value.literal: Zhao Kuangning of Xiang Prefecture had submitted since his father Deyin's time; Kuangning again communicated with Yang Xingmi and Li Keyong, and the matter was exposed.

value.zh: 七月，遣氏叔琮、康懷英攻匡凝，取其泌、隨、鄧三州。
value.en: In the seventh month he sent Shi Shuzong and Kang Huaiying against Kuangning and took Mi, Sui, and Deng.
value.literal: In the seventh month he sent Shi Shuzong and Kang Huaiying to attack Kuangning and took his Mi, Sui, and Deng prefectures.

value.zh: 匡凝請和，乃止。
value.en: Kuangning sued for peace and the campaign ended.
value.literal: Kuangning sued for peace, and the attack stopped.

value.zh: 十二月，李罕之以潞州來降。
value.en: In the twelfth month Li Hanzhi handed Luzhou over.
value.literal: In the twelfth month Li Hanzhi surrendered Luzhou.

value.zh: 二年，幽州劉仁恭攻魏，羅紹威來求救。
value.en: In the second year Liu Rengong of Youzhou struck Wei, and Luo Shaowei called for help.
value.literal: In the second year Liu Rengong of Youzhou attacked Wei; Luo Shaowei came to beg rescue.

value.zh: 王救魏，敗仁恭于內黃。
value.en: Quanzhong relieved Wei and beat Rengong at Neihuang.
value.literal: Quanzhong rescued Wei and defeated Rengong at Neihuang.

value.zh: 四月，遣氏叔琮攻晉太原，不克。
value.en: In the fourth month he sent Shi Shuzong against Taiyuan; the city held.
value.literal: In the fourth month he sent Shi Shuzong to attack Taiyuan of Jin but could not take it.

value.zh: 七月，李克用取澤、潞。
value.en: In the seventh month Li Keyong recovered Ze and Lu.
value.literal: In the seventh month Li Keyong took Ze and Lu.

value.zh: 十一月，保義軍亂，殺其節度使王珙，推其牙將李璠為留後，其將朱簡殺璠來降。
value.en: In the eleventh month the Baoyi garrison murdered its governor Wang Gong and made a gate officer, Li Fan, acting commander. Zhu Jian killed Fan and defected.
value.literal: In the eleventh month the Baoyi army mutinied, killed its military governor Wang Gong, pushed its gate officer Li Fan as acting prefect; his officer Zhu Jian killed Fan and came to surrender.

value.zh: 以簡為保義軍節度使。
value.en: Quanzhong installed Jian as governor of Baoyi.
value.literal: He made Jian military governor of Baoyi.

value.zh: 三年四月，遣葛從周攻劉仁恭之滄州，取其德州，及仁恭戰於老鴉堤，大敗之。
value.en: In the fourth month of the third year he sent Ge Congzhou against Liu Rengong's Cangzhou, seized Dezhou, and shattered Rengong at Laoya Embankment.
value.literal: In the fourth month of the third year he sent Ge Congzhou to attack Liu Rengong's Cangzhou, took his Dezhou, fought Rengong at Laoya Embankment, and utterly defeated him.

value.zh: 八月，晉取洺州。
value.en: In the eighth month Hedong retook Mingzhou.
value.literal: In the eighth month Jin took Ming Prefecture.

value.zh: 王如洺州，復取之。
value.en: Quanzhong marched to Mingzhou and won it back.
value.literal: Quanzhong went to Ming Prefecture and recovered it.

value.zh: 是時，鎮、定皆附于晉。
value.en: By then Zhenzhou and Dingzhou both stood with Hedong.
value.literal: At this time Zhen and Ding were both attached to Jin.

value.zh: 遂攻鎮州，破臨城，王鎔來送款。
value.en: He advanced on Zhenzhou, stormed Lincheng, and Wang Rong submitted.
value.literal: Thereupon he attacked Zhen Prefecture, broke Lincheng, and Wang Rong came to offer submission.

value.zh: 進攻定州，王郜奔于晉，其將王處直以定州降。
value.en: Pressing Dingzhou, Wang Gao fled to Hedong; his general Wang Chuzhi surrendered the city.
value.literal: Advancing to attack Ding Prefecture, Wang Gao fled to Jin; his officer Wang Chuzhi surrendered Ding Prefecture.

value.zh: 曾三異校定曰：三異案，唐書地理志：唐州，天祐三年朱全忠徙治泌陽，表更名泌州。
value.en: Zeng Sanyi’s collation says: Sanyi observes that the Geography Treatise of the Tang History records Zhu Quanzhong moving Tangzhou’s seat to Biyang in Tianyou 3 and petitioning to rename it Mizhou.
value.literal: Zeng Sanyi’s collation says: Sanyi notes that according to the Geography Treatise of the Tang History, in Tianyou 3 Zhu Quanzhong moved Tang Prefecture’s seat to Biyang and submitted a memorial changing its name to Mi Prefecture.

value.zh: 則是天祐二年唐州舊名猶在，至三年始更為泌。
value.en: Thus in Tianyou 2 the old name Tangzhou was still in use; it was only in the third year that it became Mizhou.
value.literal: Thus in Tianyou 2 the old name Tang Prefecture still remained, and only in the third year was it changed to Mi.

value.zh: 光化之初，未當有泌州之名。
value.en: At the beginning of Guanghua, the name Mizhou should not yet have existed.
value.literal: At the beginning of Guanghua, there should not yet have been the name Mi Prefecture.

value.zh: 今書為泌，則誤也。
value.en: So when the present text writes Mizhou, it is mistaken.
value.literal: If the present text writes it as Mi, then that is an error.

value.zh: 周德威
value.en: Zhou Dewei
value.literal: Zhou Dewei

value.zh: 天祐七年秋，梁遣王景仁將魏、滑、汴、宋等兵七萬人擊趙。
value.en: In the autumn of Tianyou 7 (910), Liang sent Wang Jingren with seventy thousand men from Wei, Hua, Bian, and Song against Zhao.
value.literal: In the autumn of the seventh year of Tianyou, Liang sent Wang Jingren with troops from Wei, Hua, Bian, and Song—seventy thousand men—to attack Zhao.

value.zh: 趙王王熔乞師於晉，晉遣德威先屯趙州。
value.en: Wang Rong of Zhao pleaded for aid; Jin sent Dewei to hold Zhao prefecture.
value.literal: The Zhao king Wang Rong begged Jin for troops; Jin sent Dewei to encamp first at Zhao prefecture.

value.zh: 冬，梁軍至柏鄉，趙人告急，莊宗自將出贊皇，會德威於石橋，進距柏鄉五里，營於野河北。
value.en: That winter Liang reached Baixiang. Zhao cried for help. Zhuangzong marched out through Zanhuang, met Dewei at Stone Bridge, pushed to within five li of Baixiang, and camped north of the Wild River.
value.literal: In winter the Liang army reached Baixiang; Zhao sent urgent word; Zhuangzong personally led the army out through Zanhuang, joined Dewei at Shiqiao, advanced to within five li of Baixiang, and encamped north of the Wild River.

value.zh: 晉兵少，而景仁所將神威、龍驤、拱宸等軍，皆梁精兵，人馬鎧甲飾以組繡金銀，其光耀日，晉軍望之色動。
value.en: Jin was badly outnumbered. Jingren’s Divine Might, Dragon Soar, and Bent Bow corps were Liang’s flower—mail and harness bright with brocade, gold, and silver, flashing in the sun. Jin soldiers looked and lost heart.
value.literal: Jin troops were few, while the armies Jingren led—Divine Might, Dragon Soar, and Bent Bow—were all Liang’s elite; men, horses, armor, and trappings were adorned with brocade, gold, and silver, shining in the sun; the Jin army gazed on them and their color changed.

value.zh: 德威勉其眾曰：「此汴、宋傭販兒，徒飾其外耳，其中不足懼也！
value.en: Dewei rallied his men: “These Bian and Song shop boys dress the part—inside the armor there is nothing to fear!
value.literal: Dewei urged his men: “These are Bian and Song peddlers—only their outsides are dressed up; within, there is nothing to fear!

value.zh: 其一甲直數十千，擒之適足為吾資，無徒望而愛之，當勉以往取之。」
value.en: Each suit costs tens of thousands—take one and it pays our march. Do not stand admiring their glitter; go and strip it from them.”
value.literal: One suit of armor is worth tens of thousands; capture it and it becomes our prize—do not stand gazing and loving it; press forward and take it.”

value.zh: 退而告莊宗曰：「梁兵甚銳，未可與爭，宜少退以待之。」
value.en: He then told Zhuangzong in private: “Liang is too sharp for a straight fight. Pull back and let them come to us.”
value.literal: He withdrew and told Zhuangzong: “Liang’s troops are very sharp; we cannot fight them yet—we should pull back a little and wait.”

value.zh: 莊宗曰：「吾提孤軍出千里，其利速戰。
value.en: Zhuangzong said: “I marched a thousand li with this lone host—speed is our edge.
value.literal: Zhuangzong said: “I have led a lone army a thousand li—my advantage lies in swift battle.

value.zh: 今不乘勢急擊之，使敵知吾之眾寡，則吾無所施矣！」
value.en: If we wait and let them count our ranks, we lose every opening we have!”
value.literal: If we do not seize the moment and strike hard, and let the enemy learn our numbers, we will have nowhere to act!”

value.zh: 德威曰：「不然，趙人能城守而不能野戰。
value.en: Dewei said: “No. Zhao can man walls, not open fields.
value.literal: Dewei said: “Not so—the people of Zhao can hold cities but cannot fight in the open.

value.zh: 吾之取勝，利在騎兵，平川廣野，騎兵之所長也。
value.en: We win on horse. Broad plain and open ground—that is where cavalry shines.
value.literal: Our victory depends on cavalry; on level plain and broad wild, cavalry is what we do best.

value.zh: 今吾軍於河上，迫賊營門，非吾用長之地也。」
value.en: Here we sit on the riverbank under their gate—that is not country where we can use our strength.”
value.literal: Now our army is on the river, pressed against the enemy camp gate—that is not ground where our strength applies.”

value.zh: 莊宗不悅，退臥帳中，諸將無敢入見。
value.en: Zhuangzong turned away displeased, lay down in his tent, and no general dared go in.
value.literal: Zhuangzong was displeased, withdrew and lay in his tent, and none of the generals dared enter to see him.

value.zh: 德威謂監軍張承業曰：「王怒老兵。
value.en: Dewei told the army monitor Zhang Chengye: “The king is furious with this old soldier.
value.literal: Dewei told the army monitor Zhang Chengye: “The king is angry with this old soldier.

value.zh: 不速戰者，非怯也。
value.en: Holding back is not fear.
value.literal: Refusing swift battle is not cowardice.

value.zh: 且吾兵少而臨賊營門，所恃者，一水隔耳。
value.en: We are too few to sit under their walls. One river is all that shields us.
value.literal: Our troops are few and we face the enemy camp gate; all we rely on is a strip of water between us.

value.zh: 使梁得舟筏渡河，吾無類矣！
value.en: If Liang ferries across, we are done for!
value.literal: If Liang gets boats and rafts across the river, we are finished!

value.zh: 不如退軍鄗邑，誘敵出營，擾而勞之，可以策勝也。」
value.en: Withdraw to Haoyi, draw them out, harry and tire them—that is how we win.”
value.literal: Better to withdraw the army to Haoyi, lure the enemy out of camp, harass and wear them down—then we can win by plan.”

value.zh: 承業入言曰：「德威老將知兵，願無忽其言！」
value.en: Chengye went in and said: “Dewei is a veteran who knows war—do not dismiss him!”
value.literal: Chengye entered and said: “Dewei is an old general who knows war—please do not ignore his words!”

value.zh: 莊宗遽起曰：「吾方思之耳。」
value.en: Zhuangzong sat up at once. “I was thinking the same thing.”
value.literal: Zhuangzong rose at once and said: “I was just thinking the same.”

value.zh: 已而德威獲梁遊兵，問景仁何為，曰：「治舟數百，將以為浮梁。」
value.en: Soon Dewei took a Liang scout and asked Jingren’s plan. “He is building hundreds of boats for a pontoon bridge.”
value.literal: Before long Dewei captured a Liang patrol and asked what Jingren was doing; he said: “He is preparing several hundred boats to make a floating bridge.”

value.zh: 德威引與俱見，莊宗笑曰：「果如公所料。」
value.en: Dewei brought the man before Zhuangzong, who laughed: “Just as you said.”
value.literal: Dewei brought him in to see Zhuangzong together; Zhuangzong laughed and said: “It is exactly as you foresaw.”

value.zh: 乃退軍鄗邑。
value.en: They pulled back to Haoyi.
value.literal: They then withdrew the army to Haoyi.

value.zh: 德威晨遣三百騎叩梁營挑戰，自以勁兵三千繼之。
value.en: At dawn Dewei sent three hundred riders to taunt the Liang camp, then followed with three thousand picked men.
value.literal: At dawn Dewei sent three hundred horsemen to strike the Liang camp in challenge, and himself followed with three thousand crack troops.

value.zh: 景仁怒，悉其軍以出，與德威轉鬥數十里，至於鄗南。
value.en: Jingren in fury marched out with his whole host. He and Dewei skirmished for miles until they reached south of Haoyi.
value.literal: Jingren in anger brought out his whole army; he and Dewei fought in running battle for several tens of li, reaching south of Haoyi.

value.zh: 兩軍皆陣，梁軍橫亙六七里，汴、宋之軍居西，魏、滑之軍居東。
value.en: Both sides formed. Liang’s line ran six or seven li—Bian and Song on the west, Wei and Hua on the east.
value.literal: Both armies drew up in formation; the Liang line stretched six or seven li; the Bian and Song troops were on the west, the Wei and Hua troops on the east.

value.zh: 莊宗策馬登高，望而喜曰：「平原淺草，可前可卻，真吾之勝地！」
value.en: Zhuangzong rode to a rise, looked out, and smiled: “Open grass and flat ground—room to press and room to pull back. This is our country!”
value.literal: Zhuangzong spurred his horse up a height, looked out, and said with pleasure: “Level plain and shallow grass—we can advance and withdraw; this is truly ground where we can win!”

value.zh: 乃使人告德威曰：「吾當為公先，公可繼進。」
value.en: He sent word to Dewei: “I will lead—you follow.”
value.literal: He then sent word to Dewei: “I will go first for you—you may follow after.”

value.zh: 德威諫曰：「梁軍輕出而遠來，與吾轉戰，其來必不暇賫糧糗，縱其能賫亦不暇食，不及日午，人馬俱饑，因其將退而擊之勝。」
value.en: Dewei urged caution: “Liang marched out rash and far. After this running fight they cannot have full rations—even if they brought food they have not eaten. By midday men and horses will starve. Hit them as they pull back and we win.”
value.literal: Dewei remonstrated: “Liang’s army came out lightly and from far away; after fighting us in running battle they surely had no time to carry provisions—even if they carried them they had no time to eat; before noon men and horses will both be hungry; strike as they are about to withdraw and we will win.”

value.zh: 諸將亦皆以為然。
value.en: The other commanders agreed.
value.literal: The other generals all agreed.

value.zh: 至未申時，梁軍東偏塵起，德威鼓噪而進，麾其西偏曰：「魏、滑軍走矣！」
value.en: Before mid-afternoon dust billowed on Liang’s east. Dewei charged with drums and cries and signaled west: “Wei and Hua are running!”
value.literal: Before mid-afternoon dust rose on Liang’s eastern wing; Dewei advanced with drums and shouts, and waved to his western wing: “The Wei and Hua army is fleeing!”

value.zh: 又麾其東偏曰：「梁軍走矣！」
value.en: He signaled east: “Liang is running!”
value.literal: He also waved to his eastern wing: “The Liang army is fleeing!”

value.zh: 梁陣動，不可復整，乃皆走，遂大敗。
value.en: Liang’s lines buckled, broke, and ran. The rout was total.
value.literal: The Liang formation shook, could no longer hold, and all fled; they were utterly defeated.

value.zh: 自鄗追至於柏鄉，橫屍數十里，景仁以十餘騎僅而免。
value.en: The chase ran from Gaoyi to Baixiang, dead heaped for miles. Jingren escaped with a dozen riders.
value.literal: They pursued from Gaoyi to Baixiang; corpses lay strewn for several tens of li; Jingren escaped with barely more than ten horsemen.

value.zh: 自梁與晉爭，凡數十戰，其大敗未嘗如此。
value.en: In decades of war between Liang and Jin, Liang had never been broken like this.
value.literal: From Liang’s contention with Jin through several tens of battles, they had never suffered defeat like this.

value.zh: 梁朱友謙以河中同州降晉，梁遣劉掞攻同州，友謙求救，乃遣存審與李嗣昭救之。
value.en: Zhu Youqian of Liang surrendered Hezhong and Tongzhou to Jin. Liang sent Liu Yan against Tongzhou; Youqian called for help, and Cunshen went with Li Sizhao to answer.
value.literal: Zhu Youqian of Liang surrendered Hezhong and Tongzhou to Jin. Liang sent Liu Yan to attack Tongzhou; Youqian called for aid, and Cunshen was sent with Li Sizhao to the rescue.

value.zh: 河中兵少而弱，梁人素易之，且不虞晉軍之速至也。
value.en: Hezhong’s army was small and weak. Liang had always despised it and never dreamed Jin would come so fast.
value.literal: Hezhong’s troops were few and weak; the Liang men had always looked down on them and did not expect Jin forces to arrive so quickly.

value.zh: 存審選精騎二百雜河中兵出擊掞壘，陽敗而走，掞兵追之，晉騎反擊，獲其騎兵五十，梁人知其晉軍也，皆大驚。
value.en: Cunshen picked two hundred elite riders, mingled them with Hezhong troops, and hit Liu Yan’s camp. They played at defeat and ran; Yan’s men chased, and the Jin horsemen turned and cut them down, taking fifty riders. Once Liang knew Jin had arrived, panic spread through the ranks.
value.literal: Cunshen chose two hundred crack horsemen, mixed them with Hezhong troops, and struck Liu Yan’s camp. They feigned defeat and fled; Yan’s men pursued, and the Jin cavalry wheeled and counterattacked, taking fifty of his horsemen. The Liang men knew Jin had come and were all greatly alarmed.

value.zh: 然河中糧少而新降，人心頗持兩端，晉軍屯朝邑，諸將皆欲速戰，存審曰：「使梁軍知吾利於速戰，則將夾渭而營，斷我餉道，以持久困我，則進退不可，敗之道也。
value.en: Hezhong’s granaries were thin and the city had only just turned; loyalties still wavered. Jin encamped at Chaoyi, and every general wanted battle at once. Cunshen said: “Let Liang see we want a quick fight and they will fortify both banks of the Wei, sever our supplies, and grind us down. Then we cannot advance or retreat. That is how armies die.
value.literal: Yet Hezhong had little grain and had only just submitted; hearts were divided. The Jin army encamped at Chaoyi, and the generals all wanted a quick fight. Cunshen said: “If Liang learns we favor speed, they will camp on both banks of the Wei, cut our supply line, and wear us down in a long stand—then advance and retreat alike become impossible. That is the road to defeat.

value.zh: 不若緩師示弱，伺隙出奇，可以取勝。」
value.en: Better to slow the march, look weak, wait for a gap, and strike from nowhere. That is how victory is won.”
value.literal: Better to slacken the march, show weakness, watch for an opening, and strike with surprise—then victory can be taken.”

value.zh: 乃按軍不動。
value.en: He kept the army in place.
value.literal: So he held the army still.

value.zh: 居旬日，望氣者言：「有黑氣，狀如鬥雞。」
value.en: Ten days passed. A reader of vapors said: “Black vapor rises, shaped like fighting cocks.”
value.literal: After ten days a diviner of vapors said: “There is black vapor shaped like fighting cocks.”

value.zh: 存審曰：「可以一戰矣！」
value.en: Cunshen said: “The moment has come!”
value.literal: Cunshen said: “We can fight now!”

value.zh: 乃進軍擊掞，大敗之，掞閉壁不復出。
value.en: He marched forward and smashed Liu Yan. Yan sealed himself in his walls and would not come out again.
value.literal: He advanced and struck Liu Yan, defeating him greatly; Yan shut himself behind his walls and did not come out again.

value.zh: 存審曰：「掞兵已敗，不如逸之。」
value.en: Cunshen said: “Yan is already broken. Better to let him slip away.”
value.literal: Cunshen said: “Yan’s army is already beaten—better to let him escape.”

value.zh: 乃休士卒，遣裨將王建及牧馬於沙苑，掞以謂晉軍且懈，乃夜遁去，存審追擊於渭河，又大敗之。
value.en: He rested the men and sent the deputy Wang Jianji to graze horses at Shayuan. Yan took it for slackness and bolted by night. Cunshen chased him to the Wei River and broke him again.
value.literal: He rested the troops and sent the deputy Wang Jianji to graze horses at Shayuan. Yan thought the Jin army was slackening and fled by night; Cunshen pursued to the Wei River and again defeated him greatly.

value.zh: 張文禮弒趙王王镕，晉遣閻寶、李嗣昭等攻之，至輒戰死，最後遣存審破之。
value.en: Zhang Wenli murdered the Zhao king Wang Rong. Jin sent Yan Bao, Li Sizhao, and others against him; one after another they fell in battle, until Cunshen was sent and broke him at last.
value.literal: Zhang Wenli murdered Zhao king Wang Rong. Jin sent Yan Bao, Li Sizhao, and others against him; they died in battle one after another, until at last Cunshen was sent and broke him.

value.zh: 豆盧革
value.en: Dou Luge
value.literal: Dou Luge

value.zh: 張文禮弒王镕，莊宗遣嗣昭討之。
value.en: Zhang Wenli killed Wang Rong. Zhuangzong sent Sizhao against him.
value.literal: Zhang Wenli murdered Wang Rong. Zhuangzong sent Sizhao to suppress him.

value.zh: 嗣昭戰歿，圜代將其軍，號令嚴肅。
value.en: Sizhao fell in battle. Huan took his army and kept iron discipline.
value.literal: Sizhao died in battle. Huan took command of his army with strict discipline.

value.zh: 既而文禮子處球等閉城堅守，不可下，圜數以禍福諭鎮人，鎮人信之。
value.en: Wenli’s son Chuchiu and others barred the city and would not yield. Huan again and again spoke of reward and ruin to the townsmen, and they trusted him.
value.literal: Wenli’s son Chuchiu and others shut the city and held firm—it could not be taken. Huan repeatedly explained fortune and disaster to the townspeople, and they believed him.

value.zh: 圜嘗擁兵至城下，處球登城呼圜曰：「城中兵食俱盡，而久抗王師，若泥首自歸，懼無以塞責，幸公見哀，指其生路。」
value.en: Huan once marched to the walls. Chuchiu climbed the ramparts and called: “Soldiers and grain are gone, yet we long resisted the throne. If we bow in submission we may not atone. Show us mercy—point us a path to live.”
value.literal: Huan once brought troops to the city walls. Chuchiu mounted the wall and called to Huan: “The city has exhausted its soldiers and food yet long resisted the imperial army. If we bow and surrender, we fear we cannot answer for our guilt. We beg your mercy—show us a way to live.”

value.zh: 圜告之曰：「以子先人，固難容貸，然罰不及嗣，子可從輕。
value.en: Huan answered: “Your father’s crime is hard to forgive—but guilt does not pass to sons, so you may be treated lightly.
value.literal: Huan told him: “For your father’s crime you can hardly expect full pardon—but punishment does not extend to successors, so you may receive lighter sentence.

value.zh: 其如拒守經年，傷吾大將，一朝困竭，方布款誠，以此計之，子亦難免。
value.en: Yet you held out a year, killed our commander, and only now, spent, offer loyalty—weigh that, and you too may not escape.
value.literal: Yet you held out for years, killed our great general, and only now when exhausted do you show good faith—weighed this way, you too will be hard to spare.

value.zh: 然坐而待斃，曷若伏而俟命？」
value.en: Still, to sit and die—is that better than bowing and awaiting judgment?”
value.literal: But to sit and await death—how is that better than bowing down and waiting for judgment?”

value.zh: 處球流涕曰：「公言是也！」
value.en: Chuchiu wept: “You speak truth!”
value.literal: Chuchiu wept and said: “What you say is right!”

value.zh: 乃遣子送狀乞降，人皆稱圜其言不欺。
value.en: He sent his son with a surrender petition. All said Huan’s words were honest.
value.literal: He sent his son with a surrender petition. Everyone praised Huan for speaking without deception.

value.zh: 既而佗將攻破鎮州，處球雖見殺，而鎮之吏民以嘗乞降，故得保其家族者甚眾。
value.en: Later another general took Zhenzhou. Chuchiu was killed, but many who had sought surrender kept their families.
value.literal: Later another general broke Zhenzhou. Chuchiu was killed, but many town officials and commoners who had surrendered were able to preserve their clans.

value.zh: 蕭希甫，宋州人也。
value.en: Xiao Xifu came from Song Prefecture.
value.literal: Xiao Xifu was a native of Song Prefecture.

value.zh: 為人有機辯，多矯激，少舉進士，為梁開封尹袁象先掌書記。
value.en: Quick-witted and disputatious, prone to extravagant provocation, he passed the jinshi in youth and served Liang’s Kaifeng governor Yuan Xiangxian as chief secretary.
value.literal: As a man he was quick-witted and disputatious, given to extravagant provocation. In youth he passed the jinshi examination and served Liang’s Kaifeng governor Yuan Xiangxian as chief secretary.

value.zh: 象先為青州節度使，以希甫為巡官。
value.en: When Xiangxian became military governor of Qingzhou, he made Xifu a circuit inspector.
value.literal: When Xiangxian became military governor of Qingzhou, he made Xifu a circuit inspector.

value.zh: 希甫不樂，乃棄其母妻，變姓名，亡之鎮州，自稱青州掌書記，謁趙王王镕。
value.en: Xifu was displeased. He abandoned mother and wife, changed his name, and fled to Zhen Prefecture, posing as Qingzhou’s chief secretary to gain audience with Wang Rong of Zhao.
value.literal: Xifu was displeased. He abandoned his mother and wife, changed his name, and fled to Zhen Prefecture, calling himself chief secretary of Qingzhou and presenting himself to the Zhao king Wang Rong.

value.zh: 镕以希甫為參軍，尤不樂，居歲餘，又亡之易州，削髮為僧，居百丈山。
value.en: Rong made him a staff officer; he liked it even less. A year later he fled to Yi Prefecture, shaved his head, and became a monk on Mount Baizhang.
value.literal: Rong made Xifu a staff officer; he was still more unhappy. After more than a year he fled again to Yi Prefecture, shaved his head, became a monk, and lived on Mount Baizhang.

value.zh: 莊宗將建國於魏，置百官，求天下隱逸之士，幽州李紹宏薦希甫為魏州推官。
value.en: As Zhuangzong prepared to found his state at Wei, fill the hundred offices, and seek hidden worthies, Li Shaohong of Youzhou recommended Xifu as legal officer at Wei.
value.literal: When Zhuangzong was about to establish his state at Wei, set up the hundred offices, and seek hidden worthies throughout the realm, Youzhou’s Li Shaohong recommended Xifu as Wei Prefecture’s legal officer.

value.zh: 任圜，京兆三原人也。
value.en: Ren Huan came from Sanyuan in Jingzhao.
value.literal: Ren Huan was a native of Sanyuan in Jingzhao.

value.zh: 為人明敏，善談辯，見者愛其容止，及聞其論議縱橫，益皆悚動。
value.en: Bright and quick, skilled in debate, he won admiration for his bearing; his sweeping arguments left listeners shaken.
value.literal: As a man he was bright and quick, skilled in discourse and debate. Those who saw him loved his bearing; when they heard his sweeping arguments, they were all the more shaken.

value.zh: 李嗣昭節度昭義，辟圜觀察支使。
value.en: When Li Sizhao held Zhaoyi, he took Huan on as observation aide.
value.literal: When Li Sizhao governed Zhaoyi, he invited Huan as observation aide.

value.zh: 梁兵築夾城圍潞州，踰年而晉王薨，晉兵救潞者皆解去。
value.en: Liang troops built the encircled fort and besieged Luzhou. After a year the Prince of Jin died, and every Jin relief force pulled away.
value.literal: Liang troops built the encircled fort and besieged Luzhou. After more than a year the Prince of Jin died, and the Jin forces sent to relieve Luzhou all withdrew.
